book: Armies of Middle-earth (Fallen Realms & Free Peoples)
content:
NTRODUCTION 
F rom the great realm of Gondor 
and the many fiefs that have pledged 
their allegiance to the White City, to the hordes of vile beings that dwell 
within the bowels of the Misty Mountains, and the swathes of Evil Men 
that inhabit the lands of Harad, Rhiin and beyond, the Third Age of Middle- 
earth has known many wars across its years, each encompassing numerous 
factions, forces and heroes as darkness continues to descend upon Middle- 
earth. Whether fighting against the onslaught of Sauron's armies to defend 
their lands against Orcish invasion, or seeking to bring ruin to the lands of 
the Free Peoples, each of these various armies have their own individual 
ways of waging war, and their own heroes, warriors and sometimes 
creatures they can call upon to fight. 
e 
'Welcome to Armies of Middle-earthTM; this guide covers many of the additional 
ki 
heroes, characters and monsters from the history of Middle-earth, beyond 
the scope of the films. Within its pages you will find a selection of profiles 
and Army Lists that will help you create armies around a number of battles or 
j 
events found within the wider world of Middle-earth, along with a series of 
thematic rules to bring them to life on the tabletop. This tome is a companion 
to the Middle-earth Strategy Battle Game Rules Manual, which you will also 
need a copy of to get the most out of this publication. You may also need a 
copy of Armies of The Lord of the RingsTM or Armies of The HobbitTM (or both) 
depending on which Army List you wish to play.

book: Armies of Middle-earth (Fallen Realms & Free Peoples)
content:
WHAT DOES THIS MANUAL CONTAIN? 
rmies of Middle-earthTM is split into three sections: Forces of Good and Forces of Evil, which showcases the profiles 
and Army Lists 
for that alignment, and the Legions of Middle-earth section, which details which Army Lists from 
Armies of The Lord of the RingsTM and Armies of The HobbitTM these profiles can be taken in. 
PROFILES 
'Within these pages you will find a number of profiles for 
the various heroes, villains, warriors and creatures from 
the wider history of Middle-earth. Each profile will feature 
the rules for that character, including their points value, 
characteristics, Heroic Actions, Wargear and any special rules 
the character has. 
'T'he profiles are split into sections roughly based on the race 
or region of the characters in question. 
ARMY LISTS 
After all the profiles for a particular alignment - either 
Good or Evil - you will find that alignment's Army Lists. 
'These are the various ways you can build your collection of 
Citadel and Forge World miniatures into Armies for Matched 
Play games. Each Army List represents a particular faction, 
alliance or group of characters that fought alongside one 
another at some point during Middle-earth's extensive 
history, and allows you to recreate those factions yourself on 
the tabletop. 
Each Army List will present all the profiles that can be taken 
as part of that Army List, along with what Wargear each 
profile can take. This is important as sometimes a character 
may have an option in their profile, but they might not be 
able to take it in a specific Army List if they did not use it at 
the point in time that the Army List is representing. 
'There may also be times where a profile is listed as requiring 
a specific piece of Wargear, and their points cost in the 
Army List will have been adjusted to include this Wargear. 
For example, in the Grief of Eomer Army List, Prince Imrahil 
must take an armoured horse and lance and so this has 
already been included in his points cost for that Army List. 
An Army List will also divide the Hero models it can include 
into the Heroic Tier they are when included in that Army 
List. Sometimes a Hero will be a different Heroic Tier in 
different Army Lists, so this is a handy reference for players 
to know which Heroic Tier all of their Hero models are. 
Each Army List will also have a selection of additional rules 
which will set out any criteria that have to be met as part of 
that Army List. For example, an Army List may need to have 
a certain Hero as its General, or perhaps a Hero can only lead 
certain Warrior models in their Warband. Whatever these 
criteria are, they will be laid out in each Army List. 
Finally, each Army List will also contain a selection of 
special rules, which will help to set them apart from other 
Army Lists. Each special rule will add character and flavour 
to the force you are playing, helping to evoke the feeling 
that you are commanding the factions from the history of 
Middle-earth! 
LEGIONS OF MIDDLE-EARTH 
Additionally, in the Legions of Middle-earth section, many of 
the profiles presented in this supplement are listed alongside 
each of the Army Lists from Armies of The Lord of the RingsTM 
and Armies of The HobbitTM they can be taken as part of, even 
though they will not be listed in those Army Lists within the 
corresponding supplement. 
WHAT ABOUT THE LORD OF THE RINGSTM 
AND THE HOBBITTM? 
Fear not fans of the films! All of the Army Lists, rules 
and profiles for all your favourite heroes, villains and 
factions from The Lord of the RingsTM and The HobbitTM 
can be found within the pages of Armies of The Lord 
of the RingsTM and Armies of The HobbitTM respectively. 
Additionally, many of the profiles found within Armies 
of Middle-earthTM will work in the Army Lists presented 
in these other supplements, providing greater depth to 
those Army Lists through the use of this publication.

At the start of the game, after both sides have deployed, Baldo may place eight 2Smm 'Irap Markers face-down on the 
board; two each of Snare 'Iraps, Iripwire Traps, Pitfall Traps, and Dummy 'Iraps. These cannot be deployed in the enemy's 
deployment zone, within 3" of another Trap Marker or an Objective Marker, or within an enemy model's Control Zone. 
'When an enemy model Moves within 1" of a Trap Marker, they immediately stop Moving and flip the Trap Marker; after 
resolving its effects, the model's Activation immediately ends. Monster, War Beast, Swarm and Chariot models are 
completely unaffected by Irap Markers, and will instead simply remove them from play if they Move within 1" of them. 
Once a'lrap has been resolved and any affected models are no longer affected, remove that Trap Marker from play. The 
effects of each 'Irap Marker are explained below: 
* Tripwire Trap - When this is revealed, Baldo's player rolls a D6. On a 2+, the model that revealed the trap suffers a 
Strength 2 hit and is placed Prone. Cavalry models that reveal a trap are only affected on a 4+. However, they will also 
be Knocked Flying in addition to the other effects. 
Pitfall Trap - When this is revealed, Baldo's player rolls a D6. On a 2+, the model that revealed the trap falls into the 
hole. Whilst in a hole, 
a model may not Move and always counts as Trapped. If a model begins its Move in a hole they 
must roll a D6; on a 4+, the model clambers out of the hole and their Move immediately ends. Cavalry models that 
reveal a trap are only affected on a 4+. However, they will also be Knocked Flying in addition to the other effects. 
Snare Trap - When this is revealed, Baldo's player rolls a D6. On a 2+, the model that revealed the trap suffers a 
Strength 1 hit, is placed Prone and is now caught in the Snare Trap. A model caught in a Snare Irap cannot Activate and 
will always count as Trapped. During the End Phase, a model caught in a Snare Trap must roll a D6; if the roll is equal to 
or less than their Strength, then they are freed from the Snare 'Irap. Cavalry models that reveal a trap are only affected 
ona 4+. However, they will also be Knocked Flying in addition to the other effects. 
* Dummy Trap - When this is revealed, the Activation of the model that revealed the Trap Marker immediately ends.

count as separate Hero models for the purpose of any special rules. If you wish to upgrade Elladan & Elrohir with horses, then 
you must purchase horses for both of the Elven twins at the given costs.

content:
BATTLE OF QYWATER 
he Shire has always been a peaceful place; the 
Hobbits that live there do not concern themselves 
with the world of the 'big-folk' or the comings and goings 
of the wider world, preferring to keep to their own lands 
and live a simple life. So, when Frodo and his companions 
set out from the Shire in their quest to take the Ring to 
Rivendell, they would have been forgiven for thinking that 
the darkness that plagued the rest of Middle-earth would 
not seep into the borders of the Shire. However, that all 
changed with the arrival of Sharkey... 
With bands of Ruffians following his commands, Sharkey 
swiftly took over rule of the Shire, putting the Hobbits to 
work and 
toil in places of industry, and enforcing 
strict laws 
and curfews upon them. When Frodo, Sam, Merry and Pippin 
returned from their quest, they found that they weren't the 
only ones to have been changed by the War of the Ring - the 
Shire, the green and pleasant land they remembered, had 
been transformed into a place of darkness, fear and misery. 
Yet the return of the four travellers brings with it 
'something that the Shire has not known in many months 
- hope. Seeing their fellow Hobbits tormented and firmly 
underneath the boot of Sharkey's Ruffians, the travellers 
rally any who are willing to their side and swiftly enact 
a plan to fight back against the tyranny that has gripped 
their home. Having found their strength and courage 
since they left the Shire, Merry and Pippin lead the Hobbits 
as they begin to rise up against the rule of 'the Chief'. 
As the Scouring 
of the Shire builds to its final conclusion, 
bands of Hobbit rebels begin to openly oppose Sharkey's rule 
and resist the Ruffians that have made their lives miserable. 
Though the Shire has rarely seen war, the events that have 
unfolded since the return of the travellers have made 
a battle 
inevitable. It is at Bywater where the Hobbits will make 
their final stand, giving their all to free themselves from the 
tyranny 
of Sharkey, in what will become the greatest battle 
in 
the history 
of the Shire. 
SPECIAL RULES 
Ambush! - Using their small stature, Hobbits can hide in the 
undergrowth before ambushing their foes. 
At the start of the game, before either side has deployed, you 
'may choose a single Warband in your Army that is not led 
by either Frodo, Sam, Merry or Pippin. The chosen Warband 
is ambushing and does not arrive as normal. Instead, at the 
end of the Move Phase on the third turn (after both sides 
have moved all their models), the ambushing Warband must 
choose one of the following: 
+ Move onto the board from any board edge via the rules for 
Reinforcements. 
+ Deploy in, or within 1" of, a wood, building, rocky outcrop 
or other similar piece of terrain that Hobbits could hide 
in. A degree of common sense is required when deciding 
which pieces 
of terrain Hobbits 
can hide in - they 
shouldn't be leaping out of a river or from behind a single 
rock! You should always agree with your opponent at the 
beginning of the game which terrain pieces are eligible 
for Hobbits to ambush from. Models deployed 
in this 
'way cannot be placed in base contact with, or within 
the Control Zones of, enemy models. Models that enter 
the board in this way do not Activate as part of the Move 
Phase, and will count as having Moved half their Move 
Value for the purposes of shooting. 
"Fear! Fire! Foes!" - As Sharkey's dominance 
over the Shire 
has grown, the Hobbits have become adept 
at finding secret 
routes between villages to move swiftly between them. 
Friendly Hobbit models gain the Woodland Creature and 
Mountain Dweller special rules. 
Heroes of the Shire - Their experiences on their travels have 
transformed Merry and Pippin from immature youngsters 
into Hobbits capable of leading their own. 
Friendly Hobbit Hero models may benefit from the Stand 
Fast of either Merry or Pippin.

ARATHORN' S STAND 
ver since the fall of Arnor and the loss of King 
Arvedui, 
the heirs of Isildur have foregone the 
title of king and instead gone by that of Chieftain 
of 
the Dinedain - a tradition first started by Arvedui's 
son, Aranarth, as he had no kingdom to rule. Each of 
these chieftains has borne the royal blood of Numenor, 
granting them the long life that the Diinedain have become 
known for. 
Centuries later, Arathorn, son of Arador, is the Chieftain of 
the Duinedain. A noble 
Man, Arathorn has led his people 
in 
protecting the lands of northern Eriador against the evil that 
still roams its many paths, hunting bands of Orcs, packs of 
'Wargs 
and older, much fouler things that might stray too 
close to the settlements and villages of the free folk that 
live under their protection. Even towns 
as far south as the 
verdant lands of the Shire have unknowingly benefitted 
from the vigilant watch of Arathorn's Rangers throughout 
theyears. 
Though rarely called upon to engage a foe in open war, 
preferring instead to unleash a hail of arrows upon those 
that seek to cause destruction, 
Arathorn and his Dunedain 
are very capable fighters, worthy of the bloodline 
that they 
hold within them. Arathorn himself is every bit as mighty a 
warrior as the kings of Numenor that he is descended from, 
and there are none within his own people that could hope to 
cross blades with him and emerge victorious. 
However, even the greatest warriors can be lured into a trap, 
and this is the fate that befell Arathorn. Having tracked the 
Hill Troll known as Buhrdiir in order to put an end to the 
beast's ravaging of the northern lands, Arathorn had greatly 
underestimated 
the cunning of his foe and found himself 
outnumbered 
and surrounded. Despite 
his skill with bow and 
blade, Arathorn was unable to withstand the onslaught, and 
he ultimately perished. However, Arathorn's bloodline 
is safe 
within his young son, who may yet grow up to be the greatest 
descendent 
of Isildur and avenge his father's death...

The Grey Company 
THE GRéY 
% 49 
ith war brewing in the land of Gondor, Aragorn 
has sent word requesting aid to the Diunedain 
of the north to ride south and join him as they make haste 
to the Pelennor. Led by Halbarad, Aragorn's kinsman, the 
Rangers of the North that join their chieftain are known 
as the Grey Company: grim-faced and hardy Men that have 
spent their lives wandering the northern lands of Middle- 
earth 
to keep it safe from the servants 
of the Dark Lord. 
'Meeting with Aragorn upon the Fords of Isen, the Grey 
Company accompanies their chieftain through the Paths of 
the Dead and onto the city of Pelargir. Here, Aragorn leads his 
kin against the Corsair fleets of Umbar, capturing their ships 
before using one to sail north up the Anduin. Arriving 
at the 
docks 
of Harlond, the Grey Company leap from the bow of 
their ship and into the Battle of Pelennor Fields, determined 
to play their part in liberating the White City. 
COMPANY 
It is not just the Rangers from the north that make up the 
Grey Company. Alongside the heir of Isildur stands his 
loyal companions, Legolas and Gimli, who have pledged 
tostay with their friend through any turmoil. Elladan and 
Elrohir have also journeyed 
south to fight at Aragorn's side, 
honouring the friendship forged in Aragorn's youth. And, at 
the head of the Grey Company is Halbarad, carrying aloft the 
Banner of Arwen Evenstar made by the Elf-maiden herself. 
Though this band of warriors that fought their way to the 
Pelennor is small, it comprises some of the greatest fighters 
of the Third Age. Heroes that will go down in legend as 
'some of the greatest in the history of Middle-earth 
should 
their quest be successful. Brave, noble, willing to sacrifice 
themselves for the greater good, and led into battle by none 
other than the true King of Gondor, the Grey Company 
will 
make for a fearsome foe for any who oppose them.

he son of King Théoden, Théodred is the sole heir

gathered a band of loyal captains and riders to his side and

to Théodred's side should the battle begin to turn ll.

cavalry charges and stoic, stubborn infantry. Led by one of 
the greatest warriors of their generation in Théodred, the 
Rohirrim fight with unparalleled courage to ensure their 
prince's safety. For so long as Théodred remains fighting with 
the fury and skill he is renowned for, his Men will follow him 
into battle against any enemy.

hen Gondor lit the beacons, calling for aid, 
Théoden pledged to answer and began to muster 
as many of the Rohirrim as he could to ride to defend the 
White City against the onslaught of Mordor. Yet the road 
to 
Minas Tirith is long, and far ahead of the Riders of Rohan 
a host of Orcs form a blockade, making it impossible to 
enter the kingdom of Gondor by conventional routes if the 
Rohirrim are to reach Minas Tirith before it is too late. 
'Making 
camp upon the edge of the Driiadan forest, Théoden 
ponders how to reach his allies in time. Yet it is here where 
the king of Rohan happens upon a chance encounter with 
the Woses, the inhabitants 
of the ancient forest, whose 
leader offers the 'Stonehouse-folk' 
safe passage through the 
forest unimpeded by the roots and trees that would normally 
make such a journey all-but impossible for the horses of the 
Rohirrim 
to move with haste. 
ok 4o 
Gladly accepting the aid of the Woses, Théoden and his people 
are led through the Driiadan by the chief, Ghan-buri-Ghan. 
Along their journey, Théoden learns of the deep hatred the 
Woses have for all Orc-kind, who have hunted their people 
for generations and destroyed areas of their forest home. In 
response, Théoden pledges to help rid the Driadan of any 
Orcs they may come across and to endeavour to drive back 
the threat of Mordor should his people reach the Pelennor. 
The Woses' vast knowledge of the forest paths is of 
invaluable use to the Rohirrim, allowing their steeds to 
traverse the undergrowth swiftly, and unleash the full force 
of their wrath upon any foes they come across. Using paths 
that only the Woses now remember, the Rohirrim 
are able to 
hunt down any Orc-folk that have strayed into the Driadan. 
The alliance between the Woses and the Rohirrim is one that 
will prove to be deadly for any who stand against them.

The Fiefooms 
THE FIEFDOMS 
atdlehdgmofmndor'spower, her rule stretched 
far across Middle-earth. 
From beyond Isengard to 
the west and to the depths of Harad 
in the south, people 
knelt to the rule of Gondor and received the prosperity 
that came with her protection. Although the royal line no 
longer sits upon the throne, and over the years of the Third 
Age Gondor's influence has been significantly reduced by 
war, there are still provinces that honour the fealty their 
ancestors swore to Gondor - these Fiefdoms will answer 
Gondor's call for aid should it ever be needed. 
Greatest amongst these Fiefdoms is undoubtedly 
the realm 
of Dol Amroth. Ruled over by Prince Imrahil, a noble lord 
descended from the line of Niumenor, Dol Amroth holds great 
sway over Gondor's 
fiefs. Though he holds no power over the 
lands outside 
his own, such is the respect 
held for Imrahil 
by the lords of other lands that they will often come to him 
seeking counsel and advice. Should Dol Amroth ever be called 
to war, Prince Imrahil will lead the Swan Knights, the pride of 
Dol Amroth's armies, into battle with honour 
and courage. 
Whilst 
Dol Amroth may 
be the most notable of Gondor's 
fiefs, 
it is by no means the only one that will come to aid the White 
City during the War of the Ring. Lossarnach also provides a 
number 
of its finest and most skilled axemen to defend the 
walls 
of the White City, and from the land of Lamedon an 
army of fearless yet reckless clansmen march to the Pelennor. 
The Men of the Blackroot Vale may not be skilled warriors in 
hand-to-hand combat, however, each of them is an expert 
marksman having honed their skills in their homeland of 
'Morthond against the Orcs that attempt to come down 
from 
the White Mountains. 
The combined might of Gondor's Fiefdoms embodies the true 
strength of the kingdom of Gondor, each complementing 
the 
others on the battlefield while excelling in their own unique 
ways 
of warfare. When called upon to defend the White City, 
the armies of the Fiefdoms will march to its defence without 
hesitation, determined to fight back the forces of Mordor with 
whatever strength they can muster 
and share in the glories 
of Gondor.

The Grief of Eomer 
THE GRIEF OF EOMER 
ith the Battle of Pelennor Fields raging on 
outside the walls of Minas Tirith, the Rohirrim 
find themselves in a desperate 
fight for their lives within 
the swirling melee. Though the Rohirrim have managed 
to 
drive back the Orcs and slowed the relentless march of the 
'Mumakil, 
the coming of the Witch-king 
and death of King 
Théoden has turned the tide against them. Even after his 
oown defeat at the hands of Eowyn, the Lord of the Nazgiil 
has laid the Shieldmaiden low, lying amongst the fallen. 
The death 
of his uncle and the perceived 
loss of his sister 
has driven Eomer to near madness with grief: In a fit of rage, 
[Eomer leads what is left of the armies of the Rohirrim in a 
final charge in a bid to rout the remaining forces of the Dark 
Lord. With only vengeance upon his mind, Eomer charges 
headlong into the fray with his loyal followers at his side. 
However, the haste 
of the Marshal of the Riddermark 
has 
caused him to overextend 
his forces and his rage has left him 
cut off from his allies. 
Yet help is close at hand; Prince Imrahil has witnessed 
[Eomer's grief and the relentless charge that has plunged him 
into the hordes of Mordor. Imrahil knows that 
if he does not 
intervene then Eomer 
will surely fall foul 
of his own wrath. 
With a swift rallying cry, the Prince of Dol Amroth commands 
the Swan Knights to follow his lead and fight their way to 
Eomer's side. 
At Imrahil's side, Hitrin the Tall gathers a band 
of nearby warriors and makes haste towards the future 
King of Rohan. 
Individually, Eomer, Imrahil and Hrin are all mighty 
warriors, 
yet together they are a truly formidable force; their 
unwavering bravery inspiring the warriors that follow them 
into battle. However, such is the fury of Eomer 
at the loss of 
his kin that his rage burns too fiercely to temper his desire for 
revenge and cease his rampage. If Imrahil and Hirin cannot 
reach him in time, then Eomer's grief may ultimately prove 
to be his own downfall, 
and Rohan will mourn the loss 
of its 
new king before 
he can even be crowned.

| ARNOR 
ver since its founding by the High King Elendil, 
Arnor has been a formidable kingdom and a bastion 
against Evil in the north. The sister kingdom to Gondor, 
Arnor was once every bit as powerful as Gondor to the 
south and shared in its Niimenorean heritage. Yet as the 
Third Age has drawn on, and the threat of Angmar has 
increased, Arnor has found itself splintered into smaller 
realms and at constant war with the armies of the Witch- 
king for over 600 years. 
As the years have rolled on, Arnor has crumbled and stands 
as but a shadow 
of its former glory, though the once-great 
kingdom of Men is still a mighty force to be reckoned with on 
the battlefield. Even as the legions of Angmar continue their 
relentless assault upon the cities and fortresses of Arnor, the 
\armies of King Arvedui fight on to hold back those who would 
see their homeland fall into darkness. Yet, no matter how 
valiant their efforts, the grinding approach toward the doom 
of their kingdom feels all but inevitable. 
Even in the final years before its ruin, Arnor boasts a 
powerful standing army that continues 
to fight to prevent 
the 
relentless advance of the forces of the Witch-king. In most 
cases, the warriors of Arnor have known war for their entire 
lives and have gained exceptional military skills through 
the necessity to survive. Donning thick-plated armour, and 
wielding 
shield and spear, those that fight for the defence of 
Arnor and their king will do so valiantly, none wanting to 
witness the last days of their kingdom. 
With times so desperate, and war seemingly without end, 
even the royal line of Arnor must fight for its survival. 
Malbeth, the king's seer, has been blessed with the gift of 
foresight and uses his power to ensure the lineage of Isildur 
endures. Even with their realm crumbling around them, when 
the combined might of Arnor marches to war there are few 
forces in Middle-earth that can stand against them; it will 
take one of the Dark Lord's greatest servants to finally see 
Arnor 
fall into ruin...

to give. In doing so, Dale must now be prepared to fight for 
their homes against the might of the Dark Lord; yet when 
they fight as a cohesive military force, the armies of Dale are 
\among the most envied in all of Middle-earth.

content:
KINGDOM OF 
e most powerful and influential of the Dwarven 
Kingdoms in Middle-earth, Khazad-duam boasted 
the greatest treasure hoard of the Dwarves of the Third 
'Age. Much of their wealth was made up of Mithril, with 
rich veins running through the heart of the mountain. 
This precious metal was used to make grand jewellery and 
items of immense value, and forged into weapons that 
would never lose their edge and armour that was as hard as 
Dragon scales. 
At its height, Khazad-dim was ruled over by Durin VI, named 
after the father of the Dwarves and marked for greatness 
from his youth. A Dwarf 
of unrivalled skill and martial 
prowess, he was claimed 
by many to be the greatest Dwarven 
warrior to have ever lived. Such was the respect commanded 
by Durin that the Dwarves he ruled over would fight for their 
liege no matter 
the cost. 
KHAZAD-DUM 
The armies of Khazad-dim were made up of hardy Dwarven 
warriors, each a fighter of exceptional skill that had been 
trained to fight since their youth. Tough warriors that made 
up the backbone 
of Khazad-diim's armies stood side-by-side 
with the likes of the elite Khazad Guard, stoic Vault Warden 
teams and the more agile Dwarf Rangers against whatever 
threats lurked within the bowels of the Misty Mountains, 
fending them off with axe and sword. 
The armies of Durin were one of the greatest forces in Middle- 
earth, and few could hope to stand against Khazad-dam's 
\awesome Dwarven might 
in open war. Under Durin's rule, 
Khazad-diim prospered like never before, and its miners 
delved ever deeper in search of new wealth. Yet 
it was this 
constant expansion that awoke something in the darkness; a 
terror so powerful 
that even the full might of the kingdom 
of 
Khazad-diim would be sorely tested against its evil.

ARMY 
OF EREBOR 
a t the time 
of the War of the Ring, Erebor has 
regained much of 
its former glory. Ruled over by 
Dain Ironfoot, wealth and prosperity have returned to the 
Lonely Mountain, and its people have flourished 
since its 
reclamation. Yet the armies of Erebor stand in a constant 
state of readiness, honing their skills to ensure that any 
attempt 
to wrest away control of the homeland is met with 
Dwarven-steel. 
At the head of the armies of Erebor stands Dain Ironfoot. 
Though ageing and past his prime, Dain is still a formidable 
warrior 
by any standard, and with his long years come vast 
experience 
and a far cooler temper than he possessed in 
his youth. At Dain's side stands his son and heir, Thorin Il 
Stonehelm; a warrior who has proven himself to be adept at 
reading the ebb and flow of battle, countering his foe at every 
turn with well-timed shifts in strategy. 
Many 
of the Dwarves of Thorin's Company made their homes 
in Erebor following their quest to reclaim it, and have taken 
up positions within its standing army. Dwalin, Gl6in, Nori, 
Dori, Bifur and Bofur have all pledged themselves to the 
service of King Dain. Even Gloin's son, Gimli, has followed 
in his father's footsteps, becoming 
an accomplished warrior 
in his own right and honing skills that would prove to be 
invaluable to the Fellowship of the Ring. 
The armies of Erebor 
boast perhaps the greatest Dwarven 
warriors of the latter years of the Third Age. Many have come 
from the Iron Hills to make Erebor their home, bringing their 
exceptional martial prowess to the Lonely Mountain. When 
called to war, Erebor's armies form nigh-on impenetrable 
walls of iron and steel which their enemies will break 
themselves upon whilst the Dwarves behind carve a path 
forwards with the finest iron-forged weaponry.

content:
DEFENDERS OF EREBOR 
e Dwarves of Erebor and the Men of Dale have been 
friends 
for many decades; the two great kingdoms 
mutually benefitting one another, with the Dwarves 
forging armour and weapons for the Men of Dale to sell 
in the city's famous markets. Following the coming 
of 
Smaug the Terrible and the Dragon's ultimate fate, the two 
kingdoms have rekindled their old alliance 
and once more 
become firm allies. 
At the close of the Third Age, it is Dain Ironfoot who rules 
Erebor. Though he is still a formidable fighter, Dain's age has 
begun to catch up with him and he is no longer 
as spry as he 
once was. His friendship with the kings of Dale reaches back 
to the aftermath of the Battle of Five Armies when Bard the 
Bowman ruled the city, and continues to this day through 
Bard's grandson, Brand of Dale. 
When Sauron sent an army of Easterlings to wage war upon 
Erebor and Dale, the two armies banded together to defend 
each other. Together their combined forces fought to save 
their homes and drive off the eastern invaders. Man and 
Dwarf fought side-by-side against their foes, striving to 
protect not only their own homelands, but also those of their 
long-standing allies. 
The combined forces of Dale and Erebor are a sight to behold. 
Rank upon rank of stubborn and heavily armoured Dwarves 
stand alongside the highly trained warriors of Dale. At the 
forefront of the armies stand the kings, Dain and Brand, 
along with their sons, Thorin Ill Stonehelm and Prince 
Bard 1l of Dale. Should their fathers fall defending each other 
in battle, then the heirs of the kingdoms 1Mill be ready to 
continue the fight against the armies of the Dark Lord. 
ADDITIONAL RULES 
* ADefenders of Erebor Army must always Include at least one Unique Erebor Hero, and at least one Unique Dale Hero. 
+ Erebor Warrior models can only be included 1n the Warband of a Erebor Hero. 
+ Dale Warrior models can only be included In the Warband of a Dale Hero. 
+ Any models with the Iron Hills keyword replace it with the Erebor keyword. 
SPECIAL RULES 
Long-standing Alliance - The kingdoms of Erebor and Dale 
have ever been close allies, and that has never been truer 
than in the closing years of the Third Age. 
Friendly Dale models within 1" of a friendly Erebor model 
'may re-roll To Wound Rolls of a natural 
1 when making 
Strikes. Friendly Erebor models within 1* of a friendly 
Dale model may re-roll To Wound Rolls of a natural 
1 when 
'making Strikes. 
'A Bond Forged in War - The friendship forged between the 
two kings 
is one that has stood for many years. Should either 
be in danger the other will risk all to save them. 
At the beginning of the Fight Phase, at the start of the 
Declare Heroic Actions step, if either 
Dain or Brand would 
be considered Trapped then the other may declare a Heroic 
Combat 
for free. If this Heroic Combat is successful, 
then 
Dain or Brand must use the following Move to join the 
other's Combat. If this is not possible, then Dain or Brand 
'must Move as close as possible to the other. A model cannot 
use this special rule if they are in the same Combat as 
the other. 
The Heirs to the Kingdoms - When their fathers perished 
upon the field of battle, the new heirs to Dale and Erebor 
continued to honour the alliance that had stood between 
their people, protecting their allies as their fathers had done. 
At the beginning 
of the Fight Phase, 
at the start of the 
Declare Heroic Actions step, if either Thorin or Bard would 
be considered Trapped then the other may declare a Heroic 
Combat for free. If this Heroic Combat is successful, then 
'Thorin or Bard must use the following Move to join the 
other's Combat. If this is not possible, then Thorin or Bard 
must Move as close as possible to the other. 
A model cannot 
use this special rule if they are in the same Combat as 
the other. 
Royal Bloodlines - The kings and heirs of Erebor and Dale 
are held in high esteem by their people and inspire them to 
great deeds on the battlefield. 
Friendly models treat each of Dain, Thorin, Brand and Bard 
asa banner.

content:
ithin the land of Mordor, the Dark Lord has 
amassed the greatest army of the Third Age, one 
capable of bringing ruin to the free lands of Middle-earth. 
It is this massive army that Sauron has unleashed upon his 
foes, with the sole aim of crushing 
his enemies under the 
onslaught of his followers and ushering in a new reign of 
terror where he holds dominion over all. 
The bulk of the Dark Lord's armies are made up of Orcs: 
vicious creatures bound in servitude to Sauron. Savage and 
bloodthirsty, the Orcs of Mordor swarm out of the Black 
Gate to wage 
war against the enemies of the Dark Lord, each 
seeking 
to earn the favour of their master. These 
Orcs are led 
by barbaric captains who have served Sauron for centuries, 
warriors who have proven to be ruthless and callous killers as 
they fight under the banners of the Great Eye. 
ARMY OF THE GREAT EYE 
Yet, there are more than just Orcs in service to the Dark Lord; 
garrisons of Evil Men known as Black Niumenoreans also 
revere him. Descended 
from those who sided with Sauron in 
the Second Age, the Black Numenoreans are said to be imbued 
with terrible magic, blessing them with an unnatural long life 
at the cost of their humanity and free will. Clad in black robes 
and sinister steel armour, these deadly warriors strike fear 
into the hearts of those who stand against them. 
At the head of the Dark Lord's armies are the Nazgul: 
Sauron's most loyal servants. When they ride 
to war, death 
and despair 
is left in their wake. Yet they 
are still beholden to 
the Dark Lord. From atop the Tower of Barad-dur, Sauron's 
gaze pierces all: a great eye wreathed in fire that keeps watch 
over his forces. None within Sauron's army can escape 
his 
sight, and those who fail him cannot hide from his wrath. 
SPECIAL RULES 
'The Great Eye - Sauron's gaze pierces armour 
and flesh, and few can escape his malign sight. 
At the beginning of the game, place a 25mm Great Eye Marker on the battlefield in your deployment zone. At the end of each 
Move Phase, remove the Great Eye Marker and roll a D6. On a 2+ you may place it anywhere within 6" of where it was. On 
a1, Sauron has been distracted and your opponent may place it anywhere within 12" of where it was. The Great Eye Marker 
can never be placed so that it overlaps another model's base, though models may finish their Move overlapping the Great Eye 
Marker. Friendly models treat the Great Eye Marker as a banner. Enemy models within 3" of the Great Eye Marker suffer a -1 
penalty to any Courage or Intelligence Tests they are required to take. 
If your opponent's Army contains a Ringbearer (with the exception of Sauron), then if during the End Phase of any turn they 
are wearing the Ring and within 3" of the Great Eye Marker, they must roll a D6. On a 3+, they succumb to Sauron and are 
immediately 
removed as a casualty.

SHARKEY'S ROGUES 
aving seen his armies defeated at Helm's Deep, 
the forges of Isengard flooded by the Ents and 
ultimately his plans for dominating Middle-earth torn 
to shreds, Saruman has been forced to flee the Tower of 
Orthanc and make his way into the wilderness. Believing 
that his downfall was initiated by the Halflings that 
spurred the Ents into action, Saruman's hatred for the 
little-folk has festered and grown, and so he has plotted 
his revenge. 
Under the guise of Sharkey, Saruman has gathered to his 
ccause bands of Ruffians from Bree and the surrounding 
lands. These cruel Men he uses to bully the Hobbits of the 
Shire, seizing their buildings and lands through extortion and 
force. Some Hobbits, such as the miller's son Ted Sandyman, 
have sold willingly, for they share Sharkey's ambition to turn 
the Shire into a place of industry and profit. 
o 
However, Sharkey cannot assume power on his own; he needs 
a puppet to be the figurehead of his operations in the Shire 
- a Hobbit that can convince the others to fall in line. To this 
end, Lotho Sackville-Baggins 
has been installed as the boss 
up in Bag End, passing laws, introducing 
taxes and sanctions, 
and allowing the Ruffians to run roughshod over his own 
kind for the sake of serving the real master behind the scenes. 
'Many Hobbits have not taken kindly to the boss' new regime, 
and some have dared to speak out against them; yet, those 
who do find themselves dragged off to the Lockholes. With 
the Shire now under Sharkey's control, bands of Ruffians are 
'@ common sight, terrorising 
the Hobbits and beating them 
if they do not follow his new, tyrannical 
rules. When the 
travellers return, Sharkey sends as many Ruffians as he can 
spare to halt them, demanding they be brought to Bag End in 
chains if they dare to resist.

book: Armies of Middle-earth (Fallen Realms & Free Peoples)
content:
MORIA 
g ok 
Yoo 
ince the fall of Khazad-dim, 
the once-great 
Dwarven realm has descended into ruin, becoming 
known as the black pit of Moria. No longer a kingdom of 
the Dwarves, Moria is now the dominion of the vile Goblins 
that swarm within 
the depths of the mountain, 
and other 
worse things. The halls that once played host to great feasts 
are now infested with Goblins and filled with the maniacal 
cackles and guttural screeches that accompany them. 
Over the centuries, countless Goblin warlords have ruled over 
Moria; yet, for almost all of them their reigns have been short, 
as they are swiftly betrayed by an aspiring rival. However, 
this is not true for the self-proclaimed 
King of Moria, 
Durburz, perhaps the largest and most barbaric of his kind. 
The tyrannical Durbiirz has managed to assert his dominance 
oover his realm, ruling with an iron fist and showing no mercy 
to those who dare to challenge his rule. 
The Goblins that now call Moria their home are a seemingly 
endless swarm. Those who stray into the dark and winding 
ccaverns will soon find themselves cornered by teeming 
hordes of Moria Goblins that seem able to attack from every 
direction, pouring through every crack and crevice large 
enough for them to squeeze through. A Goblin attack will 
be accompanied by the monotonous beat of their drums, 
heralding their advance, striking doom and despair 
into the 
hearts of those who hear the deep drumbeat.

DRrAGONS of tThe NorTh 
DRAGONS OF THE NORTH 
hroughout the long and storied history of Middle- 
earth there have been countless tales and legends 
of magnificent, 
yet terrifying creatures that have wrought 
destruction upon the lands. Creatures that tower above 
the likes of Men and Elves and possess thick, scaled 
hides, razor-sharp teeth and claws, and an intellect far 
surpassing that of mere beasts. Of all the beasts in Middle- 
earth, few are as feared as Dragons, Wyrms 
and Drakes. 
There have been many types of Dragons in Middle-earth; 
from Ancalagon, the great father of the Dragons in the First 
Age, to Scatha the Worm, scourge of the lands around the 
Grey Mountains, and the mighty Smaug, the chiefest and 
greatest calamity 
of the Third Age. Though the stories of 
these creatures of legend are well documented, it is claimed 
there are many others that still lurk within the mountain 
ranges of the northern lands of Middle-earth. 
Whilst many match the depictions in tales - huge scaled 
beasts with lashing tails and great leathery 
wings - not all fit 
this description. Those known as Drakes do not possess the 
wings that make Dragons an airborne threat. Instead, they 
are usually smaller 
and sleeker than Dragons, possessing long 
bodies and the ability to move with great swiftness across 
open terrain thanks to their lithe frames. 
Dragons and Drakes are jealous creatures, driven by their 
need to hoard gold, jewels and other items of great value. 
Though they are usually solitary creatures, keeping to their 
oown nests or lairs, should there 
be a prize too great to ignore 
they may temporarily put aside their greed and work with one 
another to claim such a treasure. The sight of one Dragon is 
likely to spell doom for any settlement, and should multiple 
Dragons have struck up an alliance then their target has little 
hope of survival.

HOST OF TéE 
\ /ITCH-KING 
n the year 1300 of the Third Age, the Witch-king, the 
Dark Lord's most trusted servant, ventured northwards 
to Angmar to seek revenge upon his master's enemies. 
Taking up residence in the fortress of Carn Dim, the Lord 
of the Nazgul held dominion over Angmar, and as his power 
grew, greater numbers of evil and twisted creatures were 
drawn out of the shadows from where they hid, to join 
his armies. 
The bulk of the Witch-king's armies are made up of countless 
Orcs, each drawn to the power of the Nazgul, and it is 
these teeming hordes that the Witch-king dispatches to 
further degrade the already crumbling kingdom of Arnor; 
eeach assault on her cities plunges her further towards the 
inevitable ruin that awaits the once-proud and regal realm 
of Men. Alongside them, Evil Men who once populated the 
mountain passes have sworn themselves to the Witch-king 
for the false promise of power. 
The Lord of the Nazgil is well-learned in the art of dark 
sorcery, and has used this malign power to bind to his will 
the essence of those long-since dead. Spirits of those that 
oonce wandered the northern paths now stir once more, each 
one called to war and utterly bent to the unyielding will of 
the Witch-king. These fell spectres join the Orcs that form 
Angmar's legions as they march to war, filling those that 
ooppose their master with dread and despair. 
Having been ravaged by centuries of war, Arnor ultimately 
fell; the might of Angmar proved to be too much for the 
remnants of this once-great 
kingdom. With Arnor now 
defeated, the Witch-king intends to unleash his full power 
on the other realms of the Free Peoples in the northern lands, 
to conquer them in the name of the Dark Lord - and unless 
they band together to face this threat, they too may suffer the 
same 
fate as Arnor.

overgrown paths of Angmar and Arnor. The howls

eengulfs the northern reaches of Middle-earth. Those that

OF ANGMAR 
At the head of each Warg pack is the alpha: the largest and 
most ferocious of all the Wargs in the region. These huge 
Wargs have earned their position through force and cunning, 
challenging the former pack leader to a fight of teeth and 
claws before feasting on the carcass of the fallen. Such a 
position demands that the alpha keeps its strength, for to 
'show weakness may encourage younger challengers to step 
forth to claim the pack as their own. 
Unlike those that are ridden by Orcs, the Wargs that form 
these Warg packs are untamed and feral. When they are 
forced to engage a foe in open conflict, they charge headlong 
towards their prey, careening into them with enough force 
to send even the most sure-footed warriors sprawling to 
the ground. There are even whispers that the Warg packs 
do not hunt alone, and that sometimes descendants of the 
Werewolves of old join them in their hunt...

hen the Lord of the Nazgil came north and

to the service of Sauron. To the Easterlings, serving the 
Dark Lord isn't just a duty but an honour, with many sects 
devoting their lives to zealously worshipping him. When 
Sauron began to amass his armies to unleash upon Middle- 
earth, the Easterlings answered without hesitation. 
The armies of the Easterlings are 
a truly impressive sight; 
highly drilled warriors clad in gleaming golden armour and 
possessing 
an exceptional martial discipline. 
Some say that 
the Easterlings clutch a blade to their chest even as they are 
weaned, whilst others claim that warfare and bloodshed is 
akin to a rite of worship in Easterling 
culture. Regardless, it is 
undeniable that the Easterlings are deadly warriors who will 
give their lives in the name of the Dark Lord. 
s fo 
As Sauron unleashes his forces upon Gondor at the Battle 
of Pelennor Fields, a contingent 
of Easterlings march to 
war against 
the Men of the West; phalanxes 
of golden-clad 
warriors armed with shields brandish long-bladed halberds 
as a wall of death against their enemies. Those 
who march 
to war at the Pelennor are led by Amdiir; an indomitable 
warrior second only to the Dragon Emperor himself and who 
commands the armies 
of the east in his stead. 
Flanked by hosts of gleaming Kataphrakts, heavily-armoured 
cavalry who ride great war horses into battle, the Easterlings 
make for perhaps the most skilled fighting force the race of 
Men has to offer. Few are able to match their raw martial 
prowess in hand-to-hand combat, and even fewer possess 
the same levels of frenzied determination that drives the 
Easterlings forwards. Under the command of Amdur, the 
Easterlings will see the kingdom of Gondor razed to the 
ground, or they will give their lives in the attempt.

THE SERPENT HORDE 
he tribes of Harad have long been at odds with 
one another; the harsh living conditions of the 
southlands have forced them to compete for water and 
resources. It is this constant quarrelling that has prevented 
the Haradrim 
from becoming 
a true power in Middle-earth; 
at least that was until the coming of the Serpent Lord. 
Through his impressive martial prowess and ruthless desire 
for power, Suladan has united the Haradrim under his 
banner 
and proclaimed himself as the Serpent Lord, growing 
his influence far greater than any other 
in the history of 
Harad. With the Dark Lord having called his followers to war, 
Suladan now leads the Serpent Horde north to the Battle of 
Pelennor Fields 
in search of riches, glory and another chance 
to cement his standing 
as the sole ruler of the southlands. 
The Serpent 
Horde is perhaps the greatest 
force of Haradrim 
of the Third 
Age. Warriors armed with bows 
and spears, 
laced with vile toxins, and raiders atop hardy horses make up 
the bulk of the army, unleashing 
a hail of poisoned arrows 
upon their foes from afar. The most skilled warriors 
make 
up the Serpent Guard: the elite bodyguards 
of the Serpent 
Lord himself. 
When the Serpent Horde is unleashed upon the plains of 
the Pelennor, their might is a fearsome 
sight to behold; 
ranks of hardy Haradrim, intent 
on razing the White 
City to 
rubble, 
are accompanied by great Miimakil 
that leave a trail 
of destruction in their lumbering 
wake. United under the 
Serpent Banner, the armies of Suladan spell almost certain 
"doom for those they face upon the field of battle.

UMBAR 
"sf?! .g::"'.""-y ' 
he city of Umbar lies upon the southern coast of 
Middle-earth. 
Though it once fell under the rule 
of Gondor, Umbar has since become an independent 
city. 
'However, Umbar is no safe haven; corruption runs rife 
through the city, where treachery and unsavoury dealings 
\are commonplace within the dark streets and shadowy 
docksides. Those who live in Umbar show little regard for 
any but themselves; for to not look out solely for oneself is 
to invite danger, treachery 
and even death. 
It has long been whispered that the lords and figureheads of 
Umbar, who on the surface seem to run the city, are no more 
than marionettes for the mysterious order of the Hasharii. 
Through 
their puppets, the Hasharii have an iron grasp over 
Umbar, controlling the flow of coin, goods and people whilst 
bending the city to their own desires. 
The armies of Umbar are made up of the Corsairs that man 
the black-sailed ships, pockets of Haradrim who have traded 
a lifeamongst the sand dunes for the stone houses of Umbar, 
and a number of Black Nitmenoreans who have dwelt within 
the city sinceit 
fell into the hands of Evil Men. Each of these 
'embodies 
the traits synonymous with the city of Umbar, 
namely greed, ambition, a ruthless streak and an inherent 
disposition towards treachery. 
Should the armies of Umbar be required to go to war, they 
will unleash a mass of disloyal and corrupt Men upon their 
foes, Men driven by greed and a desire to further their own 
goals. 
Yet hidden within the ranks of the forces of Umbar 
will undoubtedly be at least one member of the order of the 
Hasharii, sent by their hidden masters to oversee the will not 
_just of the order, but of the Dark Lord Sauron himself.

GrRAND ZArmy of The south 
GRAND ARMY OF THE SOUTH 
s Sauron prepares to unleash his full might upon 
the Free Peoples of Middle-earth, 
he calls all those 
who serve him to ready themselves for war. From the lands 
to the south, armies of Evil Men march upon the kingdom 
of Gondor, each seeking to wreak ruin upon the Men of 
the west and avenge the past defeats they have suffered 
at their hands. Men from Harad, Umbar, Rhiin and beyond 
_form together as the grand army of the south, perhaps the 
greatest army of Evil Men Middle-earth has ever seen. 
It is these amassed armies that Sauron plans to use to cut off 
the city of Minas Tirith from her allies, and reduce 
it to rubble. 
Led by the greatest warriors of their kind, these armies are 
well-prepared for war. The golden-clad Easterlings form 
nigh-impenetrable 
shield walls, whilst the Corsairs charge 
frenziedly into the fray and the Haradrim harry their foes 
from afar with hails of arrows laced with exotic toxins. 
Yet it is the great War Mimakil that make the armies of the 
south a formidable threat to the people of Gondor. These 
huge war beasts stomp across the battlefield, trampling any 
in their path as their thick hides turn aside all but the most 
determined of blows. Atop these hulking behemoths are 
hhowdabhs full of Haradrim, who shoot enemies from afar and 
pick 
off threats to the Miamakil. Should one of these beasts 
charge, even the great walls of the White City will be unlikely 
to halt them. 
Together, the combined might 
of the grand army of the south 
is a threat unlike any that has marched upon the free lands. 
Huge swathes of warriors who will zealously fight to prove 
their devotion to the Dark Lord are determined 
to bring 
Gondor to its knees - and 
if their relentless march cannot be 
halted then it is not just Gondor that will be doomed, but all 
of Middle-earth...

content: INTRODUCTION

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content:
F
rom the noble horse lords of the kingdom of Rohan, to the vile denizens of the deep that dwell within the hidden
reaches of the Misty Mountains and beyond, the War of the Ring encompassed numerous factions, forces and heroes
as Middle-earth was thrust into turmoil and war. Whether fighting against the onslaught of Sauron's armies and for their
freedom, or siding with the Dark Lord and seeking to bring ruin to the free peoples, the various armies of Middle-earth
each have their own unique fighting styles, heroes and warriors that they can call upon to muster.
Welcome to Armies of The Lord of the RingsTM; the comprehensive guide to all of your favourite factions and characters
found within The Lord of the RingsTMfilms. Within its pages you will find all of the profiles and Army Lists you will need
to create armies from your favourite The Lord of the RingsTMfilms, along with a series of thematic rules to bring them to
life on the tabletop. This tome is a companion to the Middle-earth Strategy Battle Game Rules Manual, which you will also
need a copy of to get the most out of this publication.
WHAT DOES THIS MANUAL CONTAIN?
Armies of The Lord of the RingsTMis split into two sections: Forces of Good and Forces of Evil. Each section showcases all of
the profiles and Army Lists for that alignment, which will help you build your forces and organise your collection.
PROFILES
Within these pages you will find all of the profiles for the
various heroes, villains, warriors and creatures you will be
familiar with from The Lord of the RingsTMfilms. Each profile
will feature the rules for that character, including their
points value, characteristics, Heroic Actions, Wargear and
any special rules the character has.
The profiles are split into sections roughly based on the race
or region of the characters in question. Each profile will be
divided into one (or more) Army Lists, which will explain
how you can use these characters in battle.
ARMY LISTS
After all the profiles for a particular alignment - either
Good or Evil - you will find that alignment's Army Lists.
These are the various ways you can build your collection of
Citadel and Forge World miniatures into Armies for Matched
Play games. Each Army List represents a particular faction,
alliance or group of characters that fought alongside one
another at some point during one of The Lord of the RingsTM
films, and allows you to recreate those factions yourself on
the tabletop.
Each Army List will present all the profiles that can be taken
as part of that Army List, along with what Wargear each
profile can take. This is important as sometimes a character
may have an option in their profile, but they might not be
able to take it in a specific Army List if they did not use it
at the point in time that the Army List is representing. For
example, Boromir, Captain of the White Tower, can take the
Banner of Minas Tirith in the Reclamation of Osgiliath Army
List but not in the Minas Tirith Army List.
There may also be times where a profile is listed as requiring
a specific piece of Wargear, and their points cost in the Army
List will have been adjusted to include this Wargear. For
example, in the Riders of Éomer Army List, Éomer must take
Firefoot and so this has already been included in his points
cost for that Army List.
An Army List will also divide the Hero models it can include
into the Heroic Tier they are in when included in that Army
List. Sometimes a Hero will be a different Heroic Tier in
different Army Lists, so this is a handy reference for players
to know which Heroic Tier all of their Hero models are.
Each Army List will also have a selection of additional rules
which will set out any criteria that have to be met as part of
that Army List. For example, an Army List may need to have
a certain Hero as its General, or perhaps a Hero can only lead
certain Warrior models in their Warband. Whatever these
criteria are, they will be laid out in each Army List.
Finally, each Army List will also contain a selection of special
rules, which will help to set them apart from other Army
Lists. Each special rule will add character and flavour to the
force you are playing, helping to evoke the feeling that you
are commanding the factions directly out of the films!
WHAT ABOUT THE HOBBIT?
Fear not fans of The HobbitTM! All of the Army Lists, rules and
profiles for all your favourite heroes, villains, factions and
scenes from The HobbitTMcan be found within the pages of
Armies of The HobbitTM. This publication works in much the
same way as this manual, and is fully compatible with the
Middle-earth Strategy Battle Game.
INTRODUCTION

Sent to Middle-earth by the Valar to guide the
free peoples in their fight against the Dark Lord,
Gandalf has wandered the paths of Middle-
earth since the early years of the Third Age
aiding those who have shown to have a true
heart, from Men, to Dwarves and beyond. Over
the years, Gandalf has become increasingly fond
of the Hobbits of the Shire, seeing them for the

One Ring having resurfaced within the borders
of the Shire, Gandalf has put a plan in motion
to destroy the weapon of the Dark Lord, and see
Sauron defeated once and for all.

SPECIAL RULES
Gandalf's Rockets ACTIVE - The fireworks that Gandalf carries within his cart are a spectacular sight and explode with
a loud bang in a shower of brilliant colours. However, if launched at a foe they could inflict some serious harm.

The King of Rohan during the time of the War
of the Ring, Théoden had his mind corrupted by
the Wizard Saruman, transforming him into a
wizened wreck of a Man who could barely speak
his own name. Though he suffered like this for a
number of years, it was the coming of Gandalf
that freed him from Saruman's grasp, returning
Théoden to his noble self. After leading his people
to victory at Helm's Deep, Théoden is then faced
with Gondor's call for aid; a call he answers as
he prepares his Men to ride south to battle upon
the Pelennor. Although the battle will ultimately
claim his life, the deeds done at the Pelennor will
become the stuff of legend - writing themselves
into songs to perhaps even rival those of
Théoden's forebears.

Denethor must take an Intelligence Test. If the test is passed, all is fine

Boromir be slain, then Denethor will automatically fail the next

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content:
THE FELLOWSHIP
I
n all the long history of Middle-earth, there are few
heroes as celebrated and admired as the legendary
Fellowship of the Ring. Formed at the Council of Elrond in
Rivendell, this unlikely band of nine companions pledged to
do the impossible - to journey to the depths of Mordor and
cast the One Ring into the fires of Mount Doom, destroying
it and freeing Middle-earth from the darkness of Sauron.
Led by the wandering Istari, Gandalf the Grey, the Fellowship
contained representatives from all the races of the free
peoples. From the race of Men, a ranger of the north going by
the name of Strider, and the noble Boromir from the city of
Minas Tirith. From the Dwarves, the stubborn and steadfast
Gimli, son of Glóin, a formidable warrior in his own right.
And from the Elves, Legolas Greenleaf of the woodland
realm, who would ensure that the Elves would finally see the
power of the Ring ended, as it should have been over 3,000
years before.
THE FELLOWSHIP
However, most importantly, the Fellowship contained four
Hobbits - the most unlikely creatures to join such an epic
quest. Frodo Baggins, joined by Samwise Gamgee, Meriadoc
Brandybuck and Peregrin Took, set out to deliver the One Ring
to Rivendell, only to be thrust into an adventure beyond their
wildest imaginations. For the Hobbits who had never left the
borders of the Shire, the journey would be filled with perils
they'd never encountered before, and would take every ounce
of courage they could muster to succeed.
The journey to Mordor would prove to be one fraught with
danger, and everywhere the servants of the enemy would
seek to track down and slay the Fellowship in a bid to reclaim
the One Ring for their dark master. Yet hope would endure
so long as the Fellowship stayed true to each other; though
they would each be pushed to their limits on every step of
their journey, and not all of them would live to see the end of
their tale...

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content:
THE SHIRE
T
he Hobbits of the Shire are a peaceful race, quite
content to ignore, and be ignored by, the comings
and goings of the world outside their borders. In fact, many
in Middle-earth are oblivious to the existence of Hobbits
entirely, and those that are aware of Hobbits see them as
of little or no relevance at all. Not that this troubles the
Hobbits in the slightest, and they are quite happy to just
go about their simple life without being bothered by the
'big-folk'.
On the whole, the Hobbits of the Shire live a quaint, idyllic
lifestyle away from the hustle and bustle of towns and cities,
enjoying the simple things life offers such as sampling good
food, the brewing of ales and the smoking of pipe-weed.
However, where their hearts truly lie is in peace and quiet and
good tilled earth, for all Hobbits share a love of things that
grow - and it is for these reasons that a Hobbit makes for an
excellent gardener.
THE SHIRE
Yet if there is one thing Hobbits enjoy even more than peace
and quiet, it's a good party filled with merriment, laughter
and, of course, fireworks. Perhaps the most notable of such
events was the 111th birthday of one Mr Bilbo Baggins; half
the Shire was said to be invited, and the other half seemingly
turned up anyway. Even Bilbo's disgruntled relatives, the
Sackville-Baggins, made an appearance, Lobelia proving to be
particularly unpleasant as she ranted the ear off of Bilbo.
The fireworks were provided by the wandering Wizard,
Gandalf the Grey. Gandalf has long been an ally of the Shire,
having visited its rolling green hills many times over the
years, and became known for aiding them in times of need.
However, in more recent times Gandalf has been labelled as
a disturber of the peace, possibly in relation to his part in
Bilbo's adventures with the Dragon, and him coming back far
more 'odd' than when he left. Regardless, Gandalf will still
come to the Shire should the Hobbits ever be in true need.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content:
ROAD TO RIVENDELL
ROAD TO RIVENDELL
H
aving been gifted the One Ring by his uncle,
Frodo has been tasked by Gandalf to deliver it
to Rivendell and the safety of the Elves. To accompany
him on this journey, Frodo brings with him some of his
most trusted friends from the Shire: Samwise Gamgee,
Meriadoc Brandybuck and Peregrin Took. Though they may
not be initially aware of the dangers that will face them,
the Hobbits will bravely stand by Frodo against any who
threaten him.
Upon the Hobbits' arrival in Bree, they make for the inn of the
Prancing Pony, allowed entry to the town during the pouring
rain and under the cover of darkness by the Gatekeeper of
Bree. It is within the Prancing Pony where Frodo and his
companions are able to enjoy their first good meal, large pints
and warm hearth since they set out from the Shire, all of
which are catered for them by the jolly innkeeper, Barliman
Butterbur; who also manages to secure them a pony by the
name of Bill.
Yet it is not just Barliman the Hobbits encounter in Bree.
Within the shadows of the Prancing Pony a mysterious man
is watching the Hobbits closely who, upon Frodo's mishap
and accidental slipping on of the Ring, reveals himself to be
Strider, an ally of Gandalf. This Strider seems to know about
the nature of the Ring and the terrifying Black Riders that
hunt them, and offers to help Frodo and his companions to
evade the clutches of the Nazgûl, guiding them through the
wilderness and onwards to Rivendell.
Yet even Strider can not keep the Nazgûl off their trail
entirely, and they eventually catch up to the Hobbits at
Weathertop, resulting in Frodo being stabbed with a Morgul
Blade. After driving the Nazgûl off, Strider attempts to slow
the poison, only to be caught off-guard by the Elf-maid,
Arwen. Knowing that the only chance for Frodo to survive is
for him to reach Rivendell and the medicine her father can
provide, Arwen rides with Frodo as fast as she can, though
she will need to ride as swift as the wind if she is to outride
the Nazgûl...

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content:
BREAKING OF THE FELLOWSHIP
I
t is within the sanctuary of Lothlórien that the
Fellowship came for refuge following their ordeals
in Moria, for the loss of Gandalf in the chasms of the
fallen Dwarven kingdom had left the Fellowship devoid
of direction and in need of guidance in their quest. Upon
reaching the borders of Lothlórien, the Fellowship is halted
by Haldir who has to be convinced by Aragorn to take them
to Caras Galadhon and before the Lady Galadriel.
Guided by Haldir, the Fellowship makes their way through
the woodland realm and to the great tree-city of Caras
Galadhon. Upon their arrival, Galadriel and Celeborn greet
the members of the Fellowship, offering them the chance to
rest and regather their strength for the journey ahead; and
before the Fellowship set out again they are clad in the garb
of Lothlórien, which is usually reserved for the Galadhrim
and no others, and each presented with a gift from Galadriel.
BREAKING OF THE FELLOWSHIP
The gifts bestowed unto the Fellowship are individual,
personal items that will have significance only to those they
are given to. Though they may not know it, each gift will
prove useful to the Fellowship as they continue on their quest
to save Middle-earth. Some gain weaponry to help them fight
off the perils that lie ahead, whilst others are given items
that at first glance may seem less useful, but in fact will be
integral to the success of the Fellowship.
Setting out from the safety of Lothlórien and the protection
of the Lady Galadriel, the Fellowship knows that their
toughest days are still in front of them. Yet the gifts they
have each been presented with also come with a renewed
sense of hope; hope that they may yet succeed in their heroic
quest, and hope that together they can finally bring about
the destruction of the One Ring and save Middle-earth
from darkness.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content:
KINGDOM OF ROHAN
B
efore the Wizard Saruman poisoned Théoden's
mind, the kingdom of Rohan had flourished under
its king's rule. Yet even then, Rohan found itself constantly
needing to defend its borders against bands of Orcs and
Wild Men of Dunland who sought to bring ruin upon them.
The sons of Rohan are forced to become warriors and
wield a blade far sooner than those of other races out of
necessity.
Whilst Théoden rules from the city of Edoras, his armies are
led by his royal bloodline and his most trusted marshals and
captains. The king's own son, Théodred, commands Rohan's
forces in battle, leading Éoreds of Riders of Rohan against
their enemies. The prince is a fierce and capable warrior
who has fought many battles in his short life, though his
victories have instilled a great sense of pride in Théodred,
one that can manifest as arrogance and may yet become the
prince's downfall.
KINGDOM OF ROHAN
Beneath the Prince of Rohan are the Marshals of the
Riddermark, the foremost of Rohan's warriors, with each of
them harbouring a great amount of battlefield experience
and skill at arms. Perhaps the greatest of these is Éomer, the
nephew of Théoden. An exceptional warrior and rider even by
the standards of the Rohirrim, Éomer is unshakably loyal to
his liege and will fight with all his might to protect the lands
he has sworn his life to serve.
The pride of Rohan's armies are undoubtedly her riders,
which are the envy of the races of Men across Middle-earth.
Few can boast the sheer levels of skill that the Riders of
Rohan can bring, with each one being an expert combatant
from horseback. Led by their captains, the Rohirrim will face
any enemy that threatens their lands head-on, forging their
own stories of daring and heroism that will rival even those
of their forebears and the heroic deeds they achieved during
the great history of Rohan.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content:
ROAD TO HELM'S DEEP
ROAD TO HELM'S DEEP
H
is mind now freed from the clutches of Saruman,
Théoden is made aware of all that has befallen
his kingdom. Not only has he lost his only son, Théodred,
but Rohan finds itself weakened and Edoras vulnerable
to attack. Knowing that Saruman will not relinquish his
hold on Rohan lightly, Gandalf advises Théoden to lead his
people to the refuge of Helm's Deep in order to weather the
inevitable assault from the armies of Isengard.
Seeing there to be no other option if his people are to survive,
Théoden orders Edoras to be evacuated and its people to
begin the trek to Helm's Deep. Any able men are tasked with
protecting the convoy, riding ahead to scout out the path or
holding back to ensure none of Saruman's spies are following.
Though Gandalf has gone to look for aid elsewhere, the
Rohirrim are joined by Aragorn, Legolas and Gimli, all of
whom pledge to protect the people they now ride with.
Yet the road to Helm's Deep is a long and dangerous one. The
convoy is slow and ponderous, containing many women,
children and livestock as they trudge towards Helm's Deep.
It is this that makes the Rohirrim an easy target for attack
- one which Saruman foresees. In a bid to slay the people
of Rohan and to take control of the kingdom, Saruman
commands his packs of Warg Riders to attack them
on the road.
With their enemies bearing down upon them, Théoden leads
his most capable warriors to meet them head-on - ensuring
they are fighting away from the people he is aiming to protect.
Armed with sword, spears and a steely determination, the
riders under Théoden's command crash into their enemies,
using the full force of their cavalry charge to inflict great
damage upon their foes - their sole aim to buy the people of
Rohan enough time to reach the safety of Helm's Deep.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content:
DEFENDERS OF HELM'S DEEP
DEFENDERS OF HELM'S DEEP
T
he assault upon the Westfold has forced the people
of Rohan to flee to the sanctuary of Helm's Deep;
the attack on their lands having highlighted their need
for greater protection and taller walls. Having journeyed
across Rohan and survived the ambush of the Wolves of
Isengard, the Rohirrim have reached Helm's Deep and begin
to prepare for the inevitable battle against the armies of
the White Hand.
Whilst Théoden prepares his people for the seemingly
hopeless battle that now faces them, the sound of horns calls
out across the vale. Yet this is no Orc horn, and the sound
signals the arrival of Haldir and an army of Elves from
Lothlórien. Théoden and Aragorn welcome Haldir and his
kin into the fortress and with their arrival hope is rekindled;
perhaps the combined might of Men and Elves could triumph
once more.
As the legions of Saruman's fighting Uruk-hai come into view,
the heavens open and unleash a downpour upon the fortress
of Helm's Deep. Théoden stands atop the Hornburg with his
trusted guard, ready to command his forces in the coming
battle. Upon the Deeping Wall, ranks of Men and Elves stand
side-by-side with one another, honouring the allegiance that
stood between Elendil and Gil-galad over three thousand
years ago.
Those that defend Helm's Deep are some of the greatest
warriors of the Third Age. Aragorn, Legolas and Gimli stand
upon the Deeping Wall and, along with Haldir, lead those
atop the fortress walls against the Uruk-hai below. Though it
will take every ounce of skill and martial prowess for them to
overcome the seemingly impossible odds that now face them,
Helm's Deep may once again prove to be Rohan's salvation.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content:
RIDE OUT
W
ith the Uruk-hai having stormed over the
battlements of Helm's Deep and slaughtered
many of those who had strived to defend it, it seems as
though victory is within the grasp of the armies of the
White Hand. Those who still survive have fallen back to
the keep, barring themselves within the throne room. A
sense of hopelessness and despair has begun to seep into
the minds of the survivors, and even King Théoden believes
that their time has now come.
Yet Aragorn is not ready to give up the fight. Stirring Théoden
with a moving speech of how the Rohirrim and their allies
have fought and died to defend Helm's Deep, Aragorn
convinces the king to ride out one last time against the Uruk-
hai that are attempting to break down the doors. Gathering
their horses, Théoden and his allies prepare for one final
charge in a bid to rout the fighting Uruk-hai - a charge that
will result in either death or glory.
RIDE OUT
When the time is right, Gimli lets out a great blast on the
Horn of the Hammerhand that echoes around the valley,
signalling Théoden's charge out from the doors of his keep.
Aragorn and Legolas ride alongside Théoden, felling enemies
from horseback with both blade and bow, giving their all
to deliver Helm's Deep from the onslaught of Isengard. The
king's Royal Guard are led by Gamling, who himself carries
the Royal Standard of Rohan aloft. Should this be the last
stand of the Rohirrim, then Gamling will ensure that the
king's colours fly for as long as possible.
Those who ride out alongside Théoden know that hope is all
but lost, and this will likely prove to be their doom; yet they
do so anyway in a final attempt to fight for freedom and
break the Uruk-hai that have them besieged. For it is when
the darkness is greatest that hope shines the most brightly,
and so long as Helm's Deep still has warriors willing to fight
to defend it, then it shall not fall.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content:
RIDERS OF ÉOMER
T
he siege of Helm's Deep is well underway and
things are looking bleak for the armies of Rohan.
The Deeping Wall has been breached, a section reduced
to rubble in an explosion of fire, Uruk-hai have flooded
through the walls and the defenders of the fortress have
been pushed back to the throne room. Yet even as hope is
fading for those that remain within Helm's Deep, help is not
far away - for dawn is about to break on the fifth day...
Atop the hills that surround the Deeping-coomb, the valley
that contains Helm's Deep, as the morning light begins to
crest the hills, Gandalf can be seen riding Shadowfax - and
he has brought help with him. Having found Éomer and the
rest of the exiled Rohirrim, Gandalf has led them with haste
to defend the Hornburg from the amassed armies of the
White Hand and, after riding through day and night, they
have reached the battle just in time.
RIDERS OF ÉOMER
The Marshal of the Riddermark rides with his Éored and other
loyal Rohirrim who stood by Éomer when he was cast out
under the orders of Gríma Wormtongue. Each of these riders
is a warrior of great skill and prowess, trained in the art of
warfare from horseback for many years, and have gained
great experience fighting under the guidance of Éomer. Under
the command of their Marshal, these riders have come to
liberate their kin besieged within Helm's Deep, and will give
their all to ensure they do.
With a rousing shout of 'To the King!' from Éomer, the
Rohirrim begin the rapid descent down the hill and towards
the ranks of Uruk-hai below. The timing of their arrival was
well prepared by Gandalf, for as they charge towards the fray
the morning sunlight bursts over the peaks of the hills behind
them, blinding the Uruk-hai and rendering them all but
helpless against the ferocity of the Rohan charge.

RIDERS OF THÉODEN
RIDERS OF THÉODEN
A
s the Battle of Pelennor Fields rages on, things are
looking increasingly bleak for the city of Minas
Tirith - its gates have been breached, its walls scaled and
now hordes of Orcs have begun to flood the lower levels. Yet
as dawn breaks over the Pelennor, from the north the sound
of horns can be heard ringing out across the crisp morning
air, heralding the arrival of the Riders of Théoden.
As the sun rises over the Pelennor, and the Orcs seek to press
the advantage, thousands of Riders of Rohan come into view
from over the hills to the north, their spears gleaming in the
morning sun. At the head of the army is King Théoden, clad
in his royal armour. With his men behind him and the hordes
of Mordor before him, Théoden gives a rousing speech for the
ages, one that will stir the hearts of all who ride with him to
untold acts of courage and turn even the most craven hearted
into steadfast and resolute warriors.
With a series of war cries, the king leads the charge headlong
towards the fray. At his side are his most trusted marshals
and captains: his nephew Éomer, a mighty warrior in his
prime, Gamling, the head of his Royal Guard who carries
the colours of the king aloft, and, unbeknownst to Théoden,
Éowyn rides into battle disguised as one of his riders,
carrying the Hobbit Merry with her as she does so. Each of
these will fight to the death for their king and will all achieve
acts of great heroism in the battle to come.
When the Riders of Théoden charge into battle, there are few
who can stand against their fearsome charge - its full force
is enough to smash aside shield walls, trample their enemies
underfoot and scatter those who have the sense to flee. The
sight of such an awesome charge is enough to rally any ally
to their cause with renewed hope and rout those who stand
against them.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content:
ARMY OF EDORAS
D
uring the reign of Helm Hammerhand, the kingdom
of Rohan is at relative peace. The revolts of the Hill
Tribes have been quashed, and Orc raids have become few
and far between. Yet the standing armies of Rohan remain
well trained and ready for war - for peace is a delicate
thing and it doesn't take much for it to shatter under the
right circumstances - something Helm discovers following
the death of Freca and the war his son, Wulf, brings
upon Rohan.
Helm leads the armies of Rohan in defence of its capital of
Edoras. A strong and noble warrior and a veteran of many
battles, Helm leads his army from the front. At his side ride
his two sons, Haleth and Háma, both capable fighters trained
in the art of war and skilled with both blade and bow. The
sight of the king and his heirs striding into the thick of the
fighting without fear is a sight that inspires their warriors to
steel themselves against any foe.
ARMY OF EDORAS
The enormity of Wulf's army requires that every able-bodied
Rohirrim must fight for the defence of Edoras. With the
city ablaze around her, Helm's daughter, Héra, takes up her
blade alongside Olwyn, an ageing Shieldmaiden, and Lief,
an esquire of the king, each of them stoically fending off the
armies raised by Wulf as they give their all to defend Helm's
kingdom from ruin.
The armies of Edoras are made up of the best warriors the
kingdom of Rohan has to offer. Their warriors are hardy folk
who have pledged themselves to fight for their liege and his
royal line against any foe that would threaten to raze their
homeland to the ground. Should Helm or his heirs call for
the Rohirrim to redouble their efforts, then the warriors and
riders of Rohan will fight with every ounce of strength and
fury they can muster, without a moment's hesitation; and
it would take an army at least twice their size to hope to
overcome them.
