content:
DEFENDERS OF THE HORNBURG
E
doras has fallen, the king's sons have been slain and
the few Rohirrim who survive have been driven back
to the fortress of the Hornburg where they are besieged by
Wulf's vast army of Dunlendings and Hill Tribesmen. The
loss of his sons has driven Helm Hammerhand mad with
grief, becoming a dishevelled wreck muttering under his
breath, no longer fit to rule over his subjects as he once
had; a state that sees the king seemingly disappear from
the fortress itself.
With her father no longer capable of ruling, it is his daughter,
Héra, who takes up command of the armies of the Hornburg.
With her allies Olwyn and Lief at her side to provide her with
counsel, Héra rallies those within the fortress to prepare for
war. For though she may not be the king, the blood of Helm
Hammerhand still runs through Héra's veins, and she has
been blessed to inherit his famous stoicism and natural
ability to lead.
DEFENDERS OF THE HORNBURG
Those who defend the Hornburg against the rabble of Hill
Tribesmen now camped outside their gates know that they
are facing the greatest threat to Rohan's existence in the
kingdom's history. Yet in the face of such impossible odds,
the Rohirrim refuse to simply resign themselves to defeat.
Instead, they steel themselves for the battles ahead and
prepare to give their all for the defence of their kingdom, and
to fight with every ounce of strength, courage and valour they
can muster to avenge those cut down by Wulf's armies.
Yet even in the blighted winter landscape, the defenders of
the Hornburg do not fight entirely alone. Within the blizzards
outside the fortress, an unknown force has been slaughtering
Wulf's men at night, picking off those who stray from the
camp. Though the armies of Wulf believe the so-called beast
to be a fearsome wraith, the truth is that even in madness
Helm Hammerhand is a fearsome warrior and his grief has
led him to avenge his fallen kin by any means necessary.

content:
MINAS TIRITH
MINAS TIRITH
B
efore the War of the Ring and the return of Aragorn,
the White City of Minas Tirith was ruled over by
the stewards, noble Men who were tasked with leading the
great realm following the fall of the line of kings, until such
a time that her rightful heir returned. In the final years of
the Third Age, this duty has fallen to Denethor, a Man of
noble blood though one whose desire for power runs deep;
so deep that he may well be unwilling to relinquish the rule
of the city should its king return.
Under the command of Lord Denethor, Minas Tirith's armies
have long held back the forces of Mordor, becoming the first
line of defence between the shadowed lands and the free
peoples of Middle-earth. Yet constant war has taken its
toll on Minas Tirith; the armies of the White City have run
thin with their blood being spilt in wars with Mordor. Such
conflict has also had an impact upon the steward himself,
with Denethor turning to one of the lost seeing stones for
guidance; an act that begins to crack his mind.
Though at constant war, the armies of Minas Tirith are still
a mighty force to be reckoned with. Each of their warriors is
an accomplished fighter, trained from a young age to wield
a blade and fight in formation. Clad in gleaming silver plate
and carrying thick tower shields, the warriors of the White
City form a nigh-on impenetrable bastion against the armies
of the Dark Lord, standing strong against the blades of the
enemy whenever they are called upon to fight.
Yet it is not just these warriors that make up the armies of
Minas Tirith. The most elite fighters are called up to join the
ranks of the Citadel Guard or even the Guard of the Fountain
Court. The White City also boasts an impressive cavalry
division, with each of their knights armed with finely-
balanced and razor-sharp lances. Yet it is those that lead
the city's armies that set Gondor apart from other realms of
Men; heroes such as Boromir and Faramir are amongst the
greatest the race of Men have to offer in the fight against the
Dark Lord.

A
t the eastern edges of the realm of Gondor, and
next to the land of Mordor, lies Ithilien. This once
prosperous land has become deserted and overgrown since
the fall of Minas Ithil into the hands of the dreaded Nazgûl.
Yet these lands still belong to the kingdom of Gondor, and
patrols of warriors are stationed there to keep an ever-
watchful eye upon their borders, ensuring no evil may cross
into Gondor.
At the time of the War of The Ring, it is the Steward's own son
Faramir who commands the forces of Ithilien; his followers
garrison the ruins of Osgiliath as a last line of defence
against the armies of Mordor. Stout warriors from Minas
Tirith, skilled rangers who have spent years in the wilderness
and hardy Men who have seen many battles within the city
of Osgiliath are all under the command of Faramir, and will
fight alongside him in defence of Gondor to the last man.
Along with his trusted advisors, Madril and Damrod, Faramir
leads bands of rangers into the wild lands of Ithilien, scouting
ahead and ever on watch for intruders that have made their
way into Gondor against the orders of the Lord Denethor.
Those that do seldom make it far, for Faramir and his rangers
will lie in wait hiding within the bushes and trees to strike.
The first thing intruders will know of the trap Faramir's
men have sprung is the hail of arrows that rains down upon
them, causing them to scatter before being picked off by
unseen hunters.
Yet even as the Third Age draws to a close, the forces of
Ithilien and Osgiliath remain under the constant threat
of attack. The armies of Mordor cross into their lands in
tremendous numbers, assaulting the ruined city of Osgiliath
with all their might so as to conquer Gondor's last great
bastion against the Dark Lord.

content:
RECLAMATION OF OSGILIATH
RECLAMATION OF OSGILIATH
T
he city of Osgiliath was once the great capital of
Gondor, a shining beacon of the glory of the Men of
Númenor rebuilt in Middle-earth. However, over the years
of the Third Age, Osgiliath has been the target of many
assaults from the forces of Mordor, causing it to fall into
ruin and decay, becoming a crumbling shell of its former
grandeur. Even towards the end of the Third Age, Osgiliath
finds itself home to Orc bands using it for naught more
than an outpost.
Refusing to let the former capital remain in Orcish hands,
Denethor has commanded that the city of Osgiliath must be
reclaimed for Gondor and entrusts this task to his eldest son,
Boromir. Carrying the banner of Minas Tirith aloft, Boromir
leads the warriors of the White City against the Orcs that
have infested the city, inspiring his followers to great deeds
of valour as they seek to free Osgiliath from Mordor's grasp.
Such is the fury that Boromir fights with that those that
stand against him are swiftly cut down.
At Boromir's side stands Faramir, his younger brother.
Though he is not held in the same high esteem by their father,
Faramir is still a valiant and exceptional warrior in his
own right. It is Faramir who leads the Rangers of Gondor in
the fights against Mordor, using their exceptional skills in
tracking and moving swiftly to navigate the ruined streets
and strike when they can catch the Orc armies unawares.
Individually, both Boromir and Faramir are capable fighters,
though together they are almost unstoppable.
Many of the Men who fight alongside the two brothers
have joined them on many campaigns before, becoming
knowledgeable in the battleplans and tactics employed by
the two brothers, and allowing them to fight even more
efficiently on the battlefield. Such is the loyalty that Boromir
and Faramir inspire in those they lead into battle, that when
they fight to liberate Osgiliath from Orcish hands they will do
so with a grizzled determination; so long as the sons of the
steward stand tall.

content:
ATOP THE WALLS
ATOP THE WALLS
W
ith the forces of Mordor gathered upon the
Pelennor, the city of Minas Tirith has been
besieged. With Denethor's mind having descended into
madness with the loss of his son, command of the city
and her forces has fallen to Gandalf. From atop the walls
of Minas Tirith the White Wizard now has the task of
rallying the warriors of Minas Tirith once more and steeling
their resolve.
Yet all is not lost, Minas Tirith is still a nigh-on impenetrable
fortress that has never yet been breached in its long history.
Great war machines line the walls, providing the city with
the means of fending off their attackers from afar. These
imposing Battlecry Trebuchets are designed to launch huge
chunks of rock and broken masonry towards their foes,
blasting huge holes in the formations of Mordor and bringing
down siege towers with a single hit. It is these war machines
that Gandalf hopes can stave off the advancing Mordor
forces for long enough for their allies to arrive.
However, should the walls of the city be breached, the seven
layers of the city each have huge gates, and should one level
be overrun then those who survive can fall back to the next
and the defence can begin anew. Within the city walls, the
Men of Minas Tirith will fight with renewed vigour, creating
formations within the narrower streets to force the Orc
armies away from vital areas and fighting all the harder to
protect the people who make their home in the White City.
Though command of Minas Tirith's armies has fallen to
Gandalf, he is not the only hero to stand at the defence of
the city. The Citadel Guard have joined the White Wizard in
the defence, fulfilling their duty to protect it with their lives
should the need arise. At their head is Irolas, the Captain of
the Guard, who commands his troops with an unwavering
sense of determination and courage, even in the face of such
fearsome odds. Even Peregrin Took takes up arms, standing
true to his oath sworn to the steward and fighting with all the
strength he can muster in the defence of the White City.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content:
RETURN OF THE KING
RETURN OF THE KING
W
ith the battle for the White City on the horizon,
Gondor is short of allies. Though the Rohirrim
ride south to war, their arrival may not be enough to
break the armies of Mordor; they need more men. It is
upon making camp in Dunharrow that Aragorn is met by
Lord Elrond and presented with a unique gift: the shards
of Narsil reforged into a new blade - Andúril, Flame
of the West.
Yet this gift also comes with a task; to travel the Dimholt
Road and confront those who dwell in the mountain. For
those who still inhabit the mountain halls are the spirits
of those long since dead, those who promised to aid Isildur
against the armies of the Dark Lord millennia ago, yet broke
their oath and were cursed to rot and linger onwards. Upon
reaching the depths of Dunharrow, Aragorn confronts the
King of the Dead and uses the reforged sword of the King of
Gondor to hold the dead to their oath, gaining their allegiance
for the battles to come.
When the Corsair ships pull into the docks of Harlond, it is
not an army of Corsairs that leaps off the boats but instead
a single Man, Elf and Dwarf. As the Orcs scoff at the three
foes that stand before them, Aragorn summons the Army of
the Dead to come forth, unleashing them upon the Orcs that
stand before them catching them completely unawares. The
sight of such a terrifying foe freezes the very hearts of the
Orcish ranks, allowing the Dead to cut them down where
they stand.
Upon the fields of the Pelennor, Aragorn unleashes the
deadliest army in all of Middle-earth. The shadowed legions
sweep across the Pelennor, slaying droves of Orcs, Haradrim
and Mûmakil, and they will not cease their ghostly assault
until they have made safe the city of Minas Tirith from the
armies of the Dark Lord. Such an act will serve to finally
honour what the King of the Dead swore to Isildur all those
centuries ago, allowing Aragorn to hold their oath fulfilled
and allow them to be at peace.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content:
DEFENDERS OF THE PELENNOR
DEFENDERS OF THE PELENNOR
T
he Dark Lord Sauron has amassed his armies in
Mordor, gathering to his side thousands upon
thousands of Orcs and evil Men, and is now ready to
unleash his full might upon the lands that oppose him. His
hammer blow shall fall swiftly and impact hardest against
the kingdom of Gondor; it is upon the fields of the Pelennor
where much of the future of Middle-earth will be decided,
for good or ill.
Within Minas Tirith, the forces of Gondor prepare themselves
for a war unlike any they have ever seen before. Every able-
bodied warrior is called out to fight, though they are far
outnumbered by the forces of Mordor that have amassed on
the fields outside their gates. Led by the White Wizard, the
armies of Minas Tirith are now faced with the greatest army
of the Third Age - yet they do not face this threat alone...
From the north arrives the Riders of Rohan, led by King
Théoden who has come to honour the alliance that once stood
between the two kingdoms. And from the south, Aragorn has
arrived with his companions, Legolas and Gimli, and perhaps
the deadliest army in all of Middle-earth in the spectral form
of the Army of the Dead. Even with the lower levels of Minas
Tirith overrun with Orcs, the arrival of their allies sees the
turning of their fortunes in the war with Mordor.
Together Men of Gondor, Rohan, and those long since dead
fight to drive back the armies of Mordor and to ensure that
the White City does not fall. Though the lives of many will
be claimed in the city's defence, those who do fall will be
remembered as heroes who fought in the greatest battle of
the Third Age, and stood up for what is right in the face of a
dreadful and unrelenting darkness.
ADDITIONAL RULES
Rohan Warrior models can only be included in the Warband of a Rohan Hero.
Gondor Warrior models can only be included in the Warband of a Gondor Hero or Gandalf the White.
Dunharrow Warrior models can only be included in the Warband of a Dunharrow Hero, or in the Warband of Aragorn,
Legolas or Gimli.
SPECIAL RULES
Defend the White City - Those that fought at the Pelennor have but a single goal - to ensure the White City does not fall.
Each Hero in your Army can, once per game, declare a Heroic Combat for free.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content:
MEN OF THE WEST
MEN OF THE WEST
T
hough the Battle of Pelennor Fields has been won,
the free peoples of Middle-earth do not have the time
to celebrate their victory. Though the forces of Mordor have
been driven back, the Dark Lord has not yet been defeated
and behind the Black Gate he begins to amass his forces
once more for an even greater attack upon Gondor. In
doing so, Sauron has unwittingly placed thousands of Orcs
between Frodo and the fire of Mount Doom.
Within Minas Tirith, the leaders of the armies of the free
peoples gather to discuss their options, and a plan is devised.
They hope that by marching on the Black Gate they can draw
out the armies of the Dark Lord, thereby emptying the lands
of Mordor of Orcs. Such an act will likely result in the Men of
the West all but forfeiting their own lives, but in doing so they
will be able to provide Frodo with safe passage across the
plains of Gorgoroth and one final chance to destroy the One
Ring and end the power of the Dark Lord.
Gathering their remaining strength, Aragorn and Éomer
marshal their forces and march upon the Black Gate.
Warriors of Minas Tirith and Rohan now stand side-by-side
with one another against seemingly insurmountable odds as
hordes of Mordor Orcs pour from the Black Gate. With little
choice but to give their all and fight, the Men of the West will
sell their lives dearly to enact the plan of their lords; it is only
by the courage of Men that the day can be won.
Yet the armies of Men do not stand alone, alongside them
stands Aragorn's allies and friends. Legolas and Gimli have
endured beside Aragorn since the formation of the Fellowship
in Rivendell, and Gandalf has returned to Middle-earth to
help guide those who would see Sauron fall. Even Merry and
Pippin have pledged their swords to the fight ahead. Together,
Men, Elves, Dwarves, Wizards and even Hobbits will stand
together in one final fight; the result of which will determine
the very fate of Middle-earth - for good or evil...

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content:
NÚMENOR
NÚMENOR
A
lthough they were exiles following the drowning
of their homeland at the end of the Second Age,
the coming of the Men of Númenor to Middle-earth would
change its fate forever. Founding the great kingdoms of
Gondor and Arnor to replicate the glory and splendour of
their former home, the Men of Númenor soon became a
dominant force, fighting back the armies of the Dark Lord
and becoming perhaps the greatest and most powerful
kingdom within Middle-earth.
On the throne of Gondor and Arnor sat the High King,
Elendil. Wise, noble and just, Elendil was a king beloved by
his people and ruled in a manner befitting that of the great
Númenórean kings of old. It was Elendil's desire to see his
new kingdom emulate the greatness of Númenor, a legacy
that would be carried down by his son, Isildur, and by their
descendants that shaped the kingdoms of Gondor and Arnor
for centuries to come.
The sable-clad armies of Númenor quickly became a strong
martial power. In their early years in Middle-earth, the forces
of Númenor faced evil warlords that ruled the lands, driving
the cruel Haradrim back to the southlands, and besting the
fanatical Easterlings that sought to invade from the east
- yet they prevailed in every instance, proving that their
valorous deeds and Númenórean steel could win out over
the cruelty and ruthlessness of lesser Men. However, these
wouldn't be the greatest threat to Elendil and his people...
When the hammer of Sauron fell upon Middle-earth, it was
Gondor and Arnor that felt his wrath the hardest. Bands of
Orcs raided the borders of Elendil's lands, seeking to weaken
the Men of Númenor and strike a sense of hopelessness into
them. Such was the might of the forces of Mordor that even
the armies of Númenor couldn't face them alone, and so
Elendil would have to form an alliance if his kingdom was to
survive - one that would shape the future of Middle-earth.

engage them in honourable battle.

always accept a Heroic Challenge directed at them.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content:
LINDON
LINDON
D
uring the Second Age of Middle-earth, the greatest
kingdom of the Elves is that of Lindon to the west
of the Blue Mountains. It is here where the High Elves dwell,
and are ruled over by Gil-galad, the High King of the Noldor.
The Elves have ever been the enemies of darkness and have
long fought to rid the world of the shadow of Morgoth, and
in the later Ages, that of his servant, Sauron.
Following the forging of the Rings of Power and Sauron's rise
in the latter years of the Second Age, Gil-galad knew it was
only a matter of time before war came to the Elves. Using the
power of the Ring, Sauron crushed many of the kingdoms of
the Elves, leaving a trail of ruined cities and broken bodies in
his wake. When Elendil, the High King of Gondor and Arnor,
came to Gil-galad with the proposition of forging an alliance
to challenge the rule of Sauron, it was one that Gil-galad
accepted readily and such an alliance may yet prove to be the
downfall of the Dark Lord.
Within Lindon lies the Grey Havens, the Elven port which sees
the ships sail to the Undying Lands, and it is here where the
Elf lord Círdan dwells, overseeing the Elven ships that set sail
from the port itself. Though he is well past his prime in terms
of fighting, Círdan is still more than adept with the ways of
magic, able to use his powers to aid his allies. When the Elves
of Lindon are called to war, Círdan will gather his kin from
the Grey Havens and march with them to aid the High King of
the Noldor.
At the height of their power, the armies of Lindon are without
peer within the free peoples of Middle-earth. The Elves that
make up their ranks are accomplished warriors with blade,
bow and spear, and each of them has seen countless battles
over their immortal lives. Clad in gleaming golden armour,
the sight of the armies of the High Elves is one that will make
even the bravest Orc tremble, such is the renowned martial
prowess of the Elves.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content:
RIVENDELL
RIVENDELL
O
ver the years of the Third Age, the power of the
Elves has begun to wane. Many of the Elves either
perished in the War of the Last Alliance or have sailed
west to the Undying Lands, sensing their time in Middle-
earth is drawing to a close. Though their power is greatly
diminished compared to that of the earlier Ages, the High
Elves are still a formidable fighting force and one that can
hold their own against almost any foe.
In the closing years of the Third Age, much of the remaining
power of the High Elves resides within the great Elven hall
of Rivendell. A place of peace and tranquillity, Rivendell is
ruled over by the Lord Elrond, the former ward of Gil-galad,
and is protected by Vilya, one of the three Elven Rings. Under
Elrond's rule, all manner of free peoples are welcomed into
the haven of Rivendell, so long as they show honour and
good faith to their hosts and ensure no violence is committed
during their stay.
However, as the darkness in Middle-earth grows over the
Third Age, even a place as peaceful as Rivendell must have the
means to protect itself. The armies of Rivendell emulate the
grandeur of those of earlier Ages; ranks of formidable Elven
warriors clad in elegant armour fight side-by-side, each of
them a veteran of many wars and an expert in their choice
of weaponry.
Yet where the armies of Rivendell really excel is through their
knights. These riders are amongst the greatest in Middle-
earth, with each having spent decades, if not centuries,
mastering the art of fighting from horseback. Even Lord
Elrond himself is an expert rider, often accompanying
the Rivendell Knights when the borders of their lands are
threatened by bands of Orcs or other spies of the Dark Lord.
Yet should Rivendell be truly threatened, then Elrond can
unleash the full might of the River Bruinen, causing it to
crash down upon their foes with all the fury of the sea.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content:
THE LAST ALLIANCE
THE LAST ALLIANCE
W
hen the Dark Lord Sauron forged the Rings
of Power, it wasn't long before he began to
dominate Middle-earth. One by one the free lands fell to the
power of the Ring, each of them overrun by armies of Orcs
sent by Sauron to destroy them. With each victory Sauron
grew more powerful and it wasn't long before the Dark Lord
turned his gaze towards the greater powers in Middle-earth
- yet there were some who resisted...
In order to combat the ever growing threat of Sauron, a last
alliance of Men and Elves was formed between the high
kings, Elendil and Gil-galad. Individually, both would have
been but a mere roadblock for Sauron's armies, but together
they believed themselves to be strong enough to force back
the relentless tides of Mordor and finally defeat the Dark
Lord for good.
Marching upon Mordor, the Last Alliance of Men and Elves
did battle side-by-side, and upon the slopes of Mount Doom
they fought for the very fate of Middle-earth. Man and Elf
arrayed against an Orc army that far surpassed their own in
sheer size, showing no fear as the rabble raced towards them.
Archers from both races rained arrows down upon their foes,
whilst the front ranks stood stoically waiting for the Orcs to
break upon their shield walls like waves on rock.
Though there have been many exceptional armies over the
history of Middle-earth, few have gone down in legend as
important as that of the Last Alliance. For had it not been for
the sacrifice of Elendil and Gil-galad, and the armies of Men
and Elves in defeating the Dark Lord, then the entirety of the
free lands would have been plunged into shadow, changing
the very fate of Middle-earth for the Ages to come.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content:
LOTHLÓRIEN
LOTHLÓRIEN
T
o the east of the Misty Mountains and on the western
bank of the Anduin lies the wooded Elven realm of
Lothlórien, home of the Galadhrim Elves. Unlike the dark,
twisted forest of Mirkwood, Lothlórien is a place of light,
sanctuary and healing; one where only the closest allies of
the Elves are allowed to tread. Its paths are kept clear of the
servants of the enemy, making Lothlórien one of the few
safe havens in Middle-earth during the Third Age.
Lothlórien itself is ruled over by Galadriel and Celeborn,
two Elves of immense power that have walked Middle-earth
since before the years of the First Age. Galadriel is a mighty
sorceress whose power can rival any in Middle-earth, and she
is able to keep the borders of her lands safe through the power
of Nenya, one of the three Elven Rings. Few would dare to
stand against the might of the Lady Galadriel, and those who
would will find themselves on the receiving end of her wrath.
Yet Lothlórien cannot be kept safe by the power of Galadriel
alone. It is through the martial prowess of the Galadhrim
warriors that the woodland realm has been kept free
from marauding Orc bands; something that has become
increasingly more common as the years of the Third Age have
rolled on.
The Galadhrim clad themselves in brilliant golden armour
that honours the great Mallorn trees that stand tall and
proud within the forest. It is these standing armies that
Lothlórien will need to call upon as Sauron's power grows,
whether to protect their own lands or to aid their allies in
the fights against the servants of the Dark Lord. As the sun
begins to set on the Third Age, the Elves of Lothlórien ready
themselves for war, preparing to stand alongside the free
peoples of Middle-earth one final time, now as they have
always done.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content:
FANGORN
FANGORN
A
t the close of the Third Age, Middle-earth is
controlled largely by a handful of great kingdoms,
each ruling over huge swathes of land. However, there
are still many other ancient powers within Middle-
earth, lurking within the forests and vales, free from the
commands of the realms of Men, Elves and Dwarves. Such
beings are content to simply avoid the wars and conflicts of
the wider world, keeping themselves hidden and set apart.
Of these ancient lands, the forest of Fangorn is by far the
oldest. Within the boughs of the great woodland dwell the
Ents, the tree-shepherds of Middle-earth. Often resembling
the very trees they live amongst, the Ents have been around
since before the dawn of the First Age, wandering the
woodland and forests of Middle-earth to protect them
against any evil that would seek to corrupt them. However,
in the dwindling years of the Third Age, the Ents are few in
number and have taken to residing only within the forest of
Fangorn itself.
The Ents give little to no thought to the world outside
Fangorn, instead growing weary with the weight of
millennia. As the decades have rolled onwards, the forest
has become unruly, and the Ents are too few in number to
control all the trees under their protection. With the Ents
prone to sleeping for years at a time, they were oblivious to
the rising threat of Isengard and also to the relentless march
of Saruman's flames of industry, resulting in the forest near
Isengard being ripped up to fuel its forges.
It is upon the discovery of Saruman's treachery that the
Ents are finally stirred into action. Treebeard, the greatest
of the tree-shepherds, lets forth a mighty call, rousing the
slumbering Ents from their deep sleep and summoning them
to march to war with Isengard. Though they may well be
marching to their doom, the Ents are determined to seek
revenge for their kind felled by Saruman's armies and plan
on breaking the dam and releasing the pent-up River Isen in
order to wash away the filth of Saruman forever.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content:
THE EAGLES
H
igh up in the peaks of the Misty Mountains nest the
Great Eagles. These ancient and noble beings see
themselves as above the petty squabbles and goings-on of
those beneath their lofty perch, seeing them as little more
than ants they need not concern themselves with. Yet the
Great Eagles are far more than mere beasts, possessing
an incredible intellect and fierce predatory instinct - a
combination seldom seen within Middle-earth.
As it turns out, there are few in Middle-earth that are aware
of the Great Eagles' existence, and fewer still who can say
they have ridden upon these proud beasts. The Eagles are not
quick to trust those they meet, and those that come face-to-
face with them must be cautious to prove they are an ally or
risk being torn to shreds by their huge, razor-sharp talons. It
is said that only the Wizards have earned true friendship with
the Eagles, though quite how this friendship was formed is a
mystery to all but the Istari and the Great Eagles themselves.
THE EAGLES
This friendship has proved fruitful a number of times during
the latter years of the Third Age. When the company of Thorin
Oakenshield found themselves trapped by Azog's Hunters,
it was the Eagles who rescued them from certain death. The
Eagles also came to aid the free peoples of Middle-earth at the
Battle of the Five Armies and the Black Gate, doing their part
to rid Middle-earth of darkness. When Gandalf found himself
trapped atop Orthanc, it was Gwaihir, the Lord of the Eagles,
who rescued his friend from the clutches of Saruman, flying
him away to safety.
Though the Great Eagles may wish to remain apart from the
goings-on beneath their roost, the growing threat of Sauron
means that even the Eagles will be forced to do their part for
good. For should the Dark Lord prevail and reclaim the One
Ring, then Middle-earth will be wreathed in shadow and
the Eagles will suffer the same fate as all the other races of
Middle-earth.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content:
REALMS OF MEN
WRITING AN ARMY LIST FOR KINGS OF MEN
Kings of Men are used to represent the many kings or rulers that the race of Men has had over the ages, and as such they do
not fit into any of the standard Army Lists presented within the Middle-earth Strategy Battle Game. Instead, they form their
own Army List referred to as the Realms of Men.
When writing a Realms of Men Army List, there are some things to make a note of:
Kings of Men are always a Hero of Legend. A King of Men may
include Warrior models in their Warband from any Army
List, so long as they share the same Faction Keyword.
When working out which King of Men is your Army's
General, it must be the one which shares the most common
Faction Keyword throughout your Army. For example, if
the most common Faction Keyword in your Army is Rohan,
then the King of Men with the Rohan Keyword must be
your General.
A Realms of Men Army may not have two Kings of Men with
the same Faction Keyword; however, they may have multiple
Kings of Men with different Faction Keywords.
A Realms of Men Army can never include any models with
the Unique Keyword under any circumstances. However,
it can include Hero models without the Unique Keyword
so long as they share a Faction Keyword with a King of Men
already in the Army. For example, a Realms of Men Army
with a King of Men with the Gondor Keyword could include
a Captain of Minas Tirith as they would both have the
Gondor Keyword. Hero models included in this manner may
also include Warrior models in their Warband with the same
Faction Keyword.
The Realms of Men Army List allows you to create your own
forces and combine multiple factions of Men in a way that
suits you.

It is said that a dark terror stalks the mountain pass high above Cirith Ungol, traversing its winding tunnels and hunting
any who stray into its domain. This creature is Shelob, the spawn of Ungoliant; a giant, bloated spider that has dwelt within
Mordor for millennia. Over the Ages, countless beings have been ensnared in the webs of Shelob. Yet Shelob likes to feed on
fresh, warm blood, and prefers to inject her prey with a paralysing venom, before entangling them in webbing to save for a
later time. The pass of Cirith Ungol has long been thought of as a terrible place, for few can say they have braved its caverns
and lived to tell the tale.

the land of Rhûn; a land virtually unmapped
by the Men of the West. Fanatically devoted
to the Dark Lord and his cause, these zealous

Easterling warrior is a skilled fighter and is

ruthlessly slaughtering any who would attempt
to surrender. Whilst the likes of Orcs may quiver
and flee should the battle turn ill, Easterlings
will stand and fight until the bitter end -
standing stoically in their golden armour.

The puppet of Saruman, Gríma Wormtongue
was a Man of Rohan who willingly sold his
services to the White Wizard in exchange for
promises of wealth and power. It was through
his role as Théoden's advisor that Gríma was
able to do the most harm, whispering words
of despair in the king's ear and seeing him fall
under the control of Saruman. Through the
poisonous words of Gríma, Théoden became
stripped of his will to act and only sat there
oblivious as the Westfold burned around Rohan.
Though he is no warrior, Gríma's strength lies
instead in his ability to weave words to twist the
minds of those around him, robbing even the
most wise of their heroism.
GRÍMA WORMTONGUE ................25 POINTS
WARGEAR

SPECIAL RULES
Wormtongue
PASSIVE - The tainted words spoken by Gríma provide a
combination of twisted truths and ill-serving advice.
An enemy Hero within 6" of Gríma must spend 2 Might Points rather than
1 in order to declare a Heroic Action.
A Traitor Within PASSIVE - Within the council of Edoras, Gríma's true
purpose went undetected until Gandalf rooted out his wicked ways.
Gríma can be deployed in one of two ways, though his controlling player
must decide which before either Army is deployed. Gríma can either be
deployed as part of Saruman's Warband (in which case he will not take up
a space in the Warband), or as part of the enemy Army.
If Gríma chooses to be deployed as part of the enemy Army, he must
select an enemy Hero. Once that Hero and their Warband has been
deployed, Gríma's controlling player can deploy Gríma as if he was also
part of that Warband, following all the usual deployment rules. Gríma is
still part of his controlling player's Army, and will Activate like any other
model in his controlling player's Army.
If Gríma is deployed as part of the enemy Army, then enemy models
treat him as a friendly model, and therefore cannot shoot him, Charge
him, make Strikes against him, target him with special rules, or make
a shooting attack in which Gríma would be In The Way. They may also
ignore his Control Zone. They can, however, target him with Magical
Powers like any other enemy model.
Whilst Gríma is considered a friendly model, Gríma may ignore the
Control Zones of enemy models and may Move through enemy models
as if they weren't there. When Gríma Moves this way, he cannot end his
Move overlapping or in base contact with an enemy model. Gríma can
choose to Charge an enemy model as normal if he wishes.
These restrictions immediately end if Saruman is slain, if Gríma Charges
an enemy model, if Gríma destroys an enemy Siege Engine, or if Gríma
interacts with an Objective Marker (such as destroying a Supply Marker
or picking up an objective), at which point Gríma is treated as a normal
enemy model and can be Charged, shot at and slain like any other model.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content:
The armies of Isengard that assail Helm's Deep are no mindless rabble of Orcs or Goblins, instead they are a highly drilled and
well-ordered host of fighting Uruk-hai. Alongside the Uruk-hai, huge assault ballistae are wheeled into position, prepared to
launch great bolts at those on the fortress walls. These bolts have two uses: either to impale those in their path or to have their
ends tied to great siege ladders which can then be used to raise them against the fortress - allowing hordes of Uruk-hai to
effortlessly clamber onto the walls of Helm's Deep.
ISENGARD ASSAULT BALLISTA ...........................................................75 POINTS
SPECIAL RULES
Direct Shot
Accurate
ACTIVE - An Isengard Assault Ballista will only
Scatter 3" rather than 6".
Raise the Ladders
ACTIVE - In a siege game, an Isengard
Assault Ballista can be used to raise a ladder onto enemy
battlements. To do this, choose a point on the battlements
within range, Arc of Sight and Line of Sight of the Ballista
and roll To Hit as usual. If the To Hit Roll is successful, place
a siege ladder that is within 6" of the wall base below the
target point against the battlements. A single model that
was carrying the ladder can then be placed at the top of this
ladder, and will count as Charging if there is a defender at the
top of the battlements where the ladder was raised. If not,
the model can Move as normal.
Piercing Shot
ACTIVE - A model that is hit by the shot of an
Isengard Assault Ballista will be flung back D6" directly away
from the Ballista if it has a Strength of 5 or lower. Any model
that is passed over by the flung model suffers a Strength
5 hit and will be knocked Prone. If the flung model comes
into contact with a piece of impassable terrain or a model
with a Strength of 6 or higher, then it will stop and both the
flung model and the model or piece of terrain that was hit
will suffer one Strength 6 hit. After being flung back, the
flung model will be knocked Prone if they survive. If after
the model is flung back it would finish over other models
and it has survived, then simply move the other models the
minimum distance possible to allow the flung model to be
placed where it has landed.

Moving the Charge - The Demolition Charge is a Heavy
Object on a 25mm base, and is Moved in the same manner as
any other Heavy Object.
Detonating the Charge - During the Fight Phase, after any
Heroic Combats have been resolved, a model with a torch
can attempt to detonate the Demolition Charge if they are
in base contact with it and are not Engaged in Combat. A
model may only attempt to detonate a Demolition Charge
if the resulting explosion would hit a Siege Target or at least
two enemy models. A model that wishes to detonate the
Demolition Charge must first take a Courage Test. If the test
is failed, the Demolition Charge cannot be detonated. If the
test is passed, the Demolition Charge will go off - roll on the
Detonation Table below:
DETONATION TABLE
D6
Result
1
Dud - The Demolition Charge is faulty and
does not explode. Remove it from play.
2-5
Instant Reaction - The Demolition Charge
explodes. All models (friend and foe)
within 2" of the Demolition Charge suffer
D6 Wounds. Cavalry models suffer these
Wounds on both the rider and the Mount.
Models with Fate Points or special rules that
can prevent Wounds must make a roll for each
Wound suffered; a successful roll to prevent a
Wound will only stop one, not all Wounds.
6
Titanic Explosion - The Demolition Charge
explodes as described above, with the
exception that models take 2D6 Wounds
rather than D6.
A model without a torch can still attempt to detonate a
Demolition Charge, though it will be harder to do. Any model
from the same army as the Demolition Charge can attempt
to detonate it by taking a Courage Test as described above.
However, if the test is passed, roll a D6 - the Demolition
Charge will only go off on the roll of a natural 6.
Attacking the Charge - A Demolition Charge can be shot
at and attacked as normal, and has a Defence of 7 and 3
Wounds. Each time a Demolition Charge suffers a Wound,
roll a D6. On a 6, the Demolition Charge goes off; roll on the
Demolition Table. If a Demolition Charge is Wounded by the
explosion of another Demolition Charge, it will go off on the
roll of a 4+ rather than a 6.
If a Demolition Charge loses its last Wound and does not go
off, it simply breaks and is removed from play.
If, during the End Phase of a turn, an enemy model is in
base contact with a Demolition Charge, that model hasn't
done anything during that turn except Move (i.e., has not
made a shooting attack, Cast a Magical Power, been Engaged
in Combat), and that model was not affected by a Magical
Power that turn, then it can disable the Demolition Charge -
remove it from play.

Within the tunnels and caves of the White Mountains dwell many Orcs in the service of Mordor. Constantly on the hunt for
a prized gold ring, they have no idea what their Master may want with such a trinket. Emerging from their caverns at night,
these loathsome creatures will scour the surrounding lands in search of their master's prize. Two such Orcs are Shank and
Wrot, who see the siege of the Hornburg as not only a source of food in the freezing winter, but also an opportunity to locate
the One Ring and earn the favour of their master. Shank is a slender, more conniving Orc, whilst Wrot is thick-set and dim-
witted, though particularly tough in a fight. Yet it is not just the two Orcs that scavenge through the bodies, Shank is able to
use a guttural call to summon forth a great Snow Troll that can tear through any that threaten their mission.

As the Dwarves of Khazad-dûm delved deep into the mountain in search of riches, they stumbled across a terrible evil buried
within the darkness - that of shadow and flame. A Balrog of Morgoth, a demon of the ancient world, was awoken, coming
forth from its slumber to slaughter those who had roused it. Formed of living fire and wreathed in shadow, this terrifying
creature is perhaps the most deadly of foes that any warrior could face. Able to conjure great weapons of wicked flame, there is
no mortal that could hope to stand against the Balrog and live, and even those of an older power would be sorely tested.
THE BALROG ........................................................................................350 POINTS
WARGEAR
Giant flaming hand weapon and Fiery Lash.
Fiery Lash
ACTIVE - This is a throwing weapon with a range
of 8" and a Strength of 7. Additionally, a model that is hit by
this weapon and is not slain will be removed from the board
and then placed anywhere in base contact with the Balrog,
as chosen by the Balrog's controlling player. A Cavalry model
that is hit will have the whole model dragged in this way.
If, for whatever reason, the model cannot be placed in base
contact, then it is not moved at all. If a model placed in this
way would end up in base contact with other enemy models
in addition to the Balrog, then those models do not count as
being Engaged in Combat with the placed model unless they
subsequently Charge the placed model. This is a fire-based
attack, so if a model is immune to fire-based attacks, they are
immune to this attack.
Goblin Mastery
PASSIVE - The Balrog is a terrifying being, and
the Goblins of Moria are far more scared of it than any foe.
Friendly Moria Goblin models within 6" of the Balrog
automatically pass any Courage Tests they are required
to make.
Flame of Udûn
PASSIVE - Wreathed in a burning hot flame,
the Balrog is able to manifest and control sorcerous fire.
The Balrog is never considered to be Unarmed. Additionally,
at the end of a Combat involving the Balrog, any model that
suffered a Wound from the Balrog (even if the Wound is
prevented) and was not slain must roll a D6. On a natural 6,
the model is immediately Set Ablaze. If a model is immune
to fire-based attacks, they will still suffer Wounds from the
Balrog's Strikes as normal, but can not be Set Ablaze. The
Balrog is itself immune to fire-based attacks.
Demon of the Ancient World PASSIVE - A demon from a
bygone age, the Balrog is a nigh unstoppable force.
The Balrog may declare a Heroic Combat each turn for free.
Additionally, special rules or Wargear that would slay the
Balrog instantly (such as the King of the Dead's Drain Soul or
a Morgul Blade) will only inflict half of the Balrog's starting
Wounds rather than all of them.
SPECIAL RULES
Dominant (10), Fearless, Harbinger of Evil (18"),
Large Target, Resistant to Magic, Terror

Outside the West-gate of Moria lies a still and murky pool of water, and within its depths lurks a creature of unfathomable
terror - the Watcher in the Water. Silently watching from beneath the water's surface, this tentacled creature will lash out and
strike at any who disturb the waters, dragging them to the depths or lifting them high into the air before dropping them into its
gaping maw. Quite how the Watcher in the Water came to dwell in the waters of the West-gate is one of the greater mysteries
in Middle-earth, though it is certain to have stalked many expeditions over the centuries, not least that of the Fellowship as
they came to Moria.
THE WATCHER IN THE WATER ........................................................200 POINTS
WARGEAR
Tentacles (hand weapon).
SPECIAL RULES
Dominant (6), Harbinger of Evil (12"), Large Target,
Resistant to Magic, Terror
Many Tentacles
PASSIVE - The Watcher attacks with
numerous tentacles, though should it lose a few then its
threat will become diminished.
Whilst the Watcher in the Water has 3 or fewer Wounds
remaining, its Attacks are reduced to 3.
Water Dweller
PASSIVE - A creature of the deep, the Watcher
in the Water is even more deadly whilst within the waters
it lives in.
The Watcher in the Water is never slowed when Moving
within a water feature, can still Shoot whilst within deep
water, and always counts as rolling a 6 on the Swim Chart.
Additionally, whilst within a water feature, the Watcher
in the Water increases its Move Value to 8" and gains the
Monstrous Charge special rule.
From the Deep ACTIVE - Lurking beneath the surface of the
water, the Watcher in the Water is waiting for the perfect
moment to strike.
The Watcher in the Water can never be part of another Hero
model's Warband. When you deploy your Army, do not
deploy the Watcher in the Water - keep it aside for later.
During the Priority Phase, after Priority has been determined,
the Watcher's controlling player must decide if they wish for
the Watcher to enter play. If they do, they must roll a D6 and
on a 3+ the Watcher is ready to enter play. If this roll is failed,
you must roll in each subsequent Priority Phase until the
Watcher is ready to enter play.
When the Watcher is ready to enter play, immediately place
it anywhere on the battlefield; however, the Watcher cannot
displace other models when it enters play in this manner.
The Watcher in the Water cannot Charge on the turn in
which it arrives, but may otherwise act normally.

BRUTAL POWER ATTACK - When the
opportunity presents itself, the Watcher will wrap a slimy

can still make these shooting attacks whilst it is Engaged
in Combat.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content:
BARAD-DÛR
I
t was during the years of the Second Age that the Dark
Lord Sauron rose to full power. Though he had helped the
free peoples create the Rings of Power, it was within the
lands of Mordor where he forged for himself a master Ring
to rule all others. Into this he poured his malice, his cruelty
and his will to dominate all life, and through the power of
the One Ring Sauron set out to conquer all of Middle-earth.
The armies of the Dark Lord are filled with creatures bound
to his indomitable will. Legions of Orcs swarm the plains of
Mordor, multiplying at horrific speeds and swelling Sauron's
forces. Armed with crude weaponry and plated in whatever
scraps of metal the forges of Mordor can spare, these Orcs
make up the bulk of the armies of Mordor and are sent in
huge numbers to wage war upon the enemies of the Dark
Lord, bringing death and ruin to the free peoples in their
master's name.
BARAD-DÛR
However, there are more than just mere Orcs within Sauron's
ranks. Vicious Wargs race into battle with their riders atop
them, tearing at their foes with razor-sharp teeth and claws.
Huge, monstrous Trolls stride into battle wielding massive
cleavers or clubs, protected by thick scales and even thicker
armour. And then there are the Nazgûl - Sauron's most
deadly of servants. Deceived and corrupted by Sauron, these
wraith-like beings now serve the Dark Lord unwaveringly.
During the War of the Last Alliance, the Dark Lord himself
strode into battle against the armies of Men and Elves. Such
was the might of Sauron that none could stand against
him, smashing aside his foes with great swings of his mace.
Even the high kings Elendil and Gil-galad could not bring
him down, and were felled by the Dark Lord's fury. Only by
separating the One Ring from its master could its power
be undone...

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content:
THE BLACK RIDERS
T
he Dark Lord Sauron created a series of rings
containing enough power to govern the free peoples
of Middle-earth. Nine of these were given to kings of Men
as a gift so that they could rule justly over their people,
a gift they each readily accepted. However, they were all
deceived. Sauron had forged in secret a master ring to
control all others, and soon the once great kings of Men fell
to the power of the rings they had taken.
Now helpless slaves to the power of Sauron and the One Ring,
these Men no longer resemble the noble kings they had once
been. Instead they have become twisted into the Ringwraiths;
shadowed, spirit-like beings that serve the Dark Lord
unwaveringly, and every ounce of their free will was stripped
away millennia ago. They are sustained by the power of the
Ring, and whilst it exists they cannot be truly killed.
Upon torturing the creature Gollum, the Ringwraiths
discerned two words - 'Shire' and 'Baggins'. With this
new lead, Sauron has dispatched the Black Riders to travel
northwards to the Shire, find this Baggins and retrieve
the One Ring from their grasp. At all times they sense the
presence of the Ring and will never stop hunting the one
who carries it. Their hunt for the Ring drives them onwards,
sustained by its power.
The Black Riders are the deadliest and most devoted servants
of the Dark Lord, bound to his will for all time. Cloaked in
black robes and seeming to possess no physical form, the
Ringwraiths are a terrifying foe that will relentlessly track the
Ringbearer to return the Ring to their master. The shriek of
the Nazgûl is a chilling sound unlike any other, able to invoke
untold terror in any who hear it.
THE BLACK RIDERS

Screech of the Nazgûl - Piercing through the blackness,

other; filling those who hear it with an eerie sense of dread.
A friendly Ringwraith model can use this special rule at the

model is immediately subject to the Transfix Magical Power,

The Will of Sauron - Having sent the Nazgûl to hunt
down and locate the One Ring, Sauron has put his all into
sustaining them.
Friendly Ringwraith models do not lose a Will Point for
being Engaged in Combat as per the Will of Evil special rule.
Hunt the Ringbearer - The Nazgûl will never stop hunting
for the Ring, and when it is near they will strive to retrieve it
at all costs.
At the start of the Fight Phase, before any other Heroic
Actions are declared, a single friendly Ringwraith may
declare a Heroic Combat for free. This can only be done if,
should the Heroic Combat be successful, the Ringwraith
could Charge the Ringbearer. If the Heroic Combat is
successful, the Ringwraith must Charge the Ringbearer,
though any other models involved in the Heroic Combat may
act as normal.
If both players declare a Heroic Combat in the Fight Phase in
which this special rule is used, this player will automatically
win the roll-off to see which Heroic Combat goes first;
however, this Heroic Combat declared by this special rule
must be the one chosen to go first.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content:
WRAITHS ON WINGS
WRAITHS ON WINGS
W
hen the Nazgûl were sent forth from Minas
Morgul to hunt the One Ring, they did so from
the back of their dark steeds. Pursuing the Ringbearer
from horseback, the Nazgûl chased Frodo all the way
to the Bruinen, where the magic of Arwen invoked the
great power of the river, calling it forth to wash away the
Nazgûl. In doing so the Ringwraiths were left without their
steeds - yet they had far more powerful beasts waiting
within Mordor...
Setting out once more from the black lands, the Nazgûl do so
this time from atop their monstrous Fell Beasts, for secrecy
is no longer a luxury the Dark Lord can afford. These huge
winged creatures are amongst the most terrifying in all
of Mordor. Long necks protrude out from their bodies, and
their maws are filled with rows of razor-sharp teeth. Their
leathery wings span great distances, shrouding those below
in shadow, and their talons are capable of piercing armour
with frightening ease.
From atop their Fell Beasts, the Nazgûl can cover vast
swathes of Middle-earth with great swiftness, quickly
scouring the lands below them in search of the Ringbearer,
travelling many leagues in a short space of time. The cry
of a Fell Beast is a truly horrific sound, a guttural and
primal screech that cuts through the resolve of all who
hear it, freezing the hearts of even the bravest and most
stalwart warrior.
Should a Fell Beast give chase to its quarry, no horse, Warg
or other mount can hope to outrun them, escaping only if
the creature should turn its attention elsewhere. Such is the
might of these winged creatures that they can use their huge
talons to destroy war machines or grasp many enemies in
one go, either crushing them or lifting them high into the
air before releasing them to plummet to their deaths below.
Such is the terror of the Fell Beasts that it should come as
little wonder that they make for the perfect mounts of untold
horror for the deadliest of Sauron's servants.

The first time a friendly Monster model Charges during its

no longer Engaged in Combat, it may continue its Activation
and may even Charge again if it wishes; though if it does, any
subsequent Charges will not confer this effect.

will likely grasp at those beneath in an attempt to crush them
within its huge claws.
At the end of a friendly Monster model's Move, if it is not

hit and, if it survives, will be knocked Prone. Cavalry models
suffer these hits on both the Mount and the rider.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content:
ARMY OF GOTHMOG
ARMY OF GOTHMOG
A
t the close of the Third Age, Sauron prepares to
wage open war upon the free peoples of Middle-
earth. His hammer will fall first and hardest upon the city
of Minas Tirith and the kingdom of Gondor, who have long
opposed the Dark Lord. To bring ruin to the race of Men,
Sauron unleashes the greatest army of Orcs he can muster,
sent with the sole purpose of razing the White City to
the ground.
At the head of this army is his lieutenant, Gothmog, the
highest ranking Orc in the service of the Dark Lord. Though he
is scarred and no longer the formidable warrior he once was,
this cruel and twisted Orc is without peer within the armies
of Mordor. Few Orcs possess the keen grasp of battle tactics
that Gothmog boasts, for he is the master of any battlefield
he steps onto. Commanding the forces of Mordor with a
ruthless tenacity, Gothmog's sole purpose is now to end the
race of Men.
Within Gothmog's grand army are amassed legions of
Morannon Orcs; stronger and tougher than the standard
Mordor Orcs, these vicious killers are clad in thicker armour
and carry keener weapons than their counterparts. Striding
alongside the Orcs are the hulking Mordor Trolls; some wield
great weapons to smash down walls and crush their enemies,
whilst others push great war machines into battle that will
be used to rain down huge rocks upon the battlements of
Minas Tirith.
It is these forces that stormed the city of Osgiliath,
overrunning it and bringing death to those who sought to
defend it, claiming it for the Dark Lord once more. Following
the sacking of Osgiliath, Gothmog has unleashed his armies
upon Minas Tirith in the greatest battle of the Third Age.
Such is the might of the army of Gothmog that it would take
the combined armies of the free peoples to halt its relentless
march and overcome it.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content:
LEGIONS OF MORDOR
LEGIONS OF MORDOR
T
he Dark Lord Sauron has amassed his armies in
Mordor, gathering to his side thousands upon
thousands of Orcs and evil Men, and is now ready to
unleash his full might upon the lands that oppose him. It
is the kingdom of Gondor that is the target for his fury,
and it is upon the fields of the Pelennor where the legions
of Mordor shall bring their full might to bear against the
enemies of the Dark Lord.
A huge army of Orcs the likes of which has never been seen
in Middle-earth has been amassed, and is now prepared
to assail the White City with the purpose of seeing it in
flames and reduced to rubble. Led by the great Orc tactician,
Gothmog, these Orcs are the best equipped and most well
armed of all the Orcs in the service of Sauron; and they will
attack with their full fury to crush the race of Men and usher
in the time of the Orc.
Sauron has more than Orcs in his service. From the south
marches an army of Haradrim: bands of tribal warriors
riding atop great Mûmakil and trampling any who lie in their
path. From the lands of Rhûn the Easterlings have joined the
Dark Lord's cause, each a fanatical warrior with a zealous
devotion to Sauron and possessing exceptional martial skill.
Together, these forces seek to spell the doom of Minas Tirith
and those who have pledged their lives to defend it.
Yet in overall command of the legions of Mordor is Sauron's
deadliest and most loyal servant, one who has served his
master for centuries and now commands the greatest
battle in the Dark Lord's name - the dreaded Witch-king of
Angmar. With such a fearsome foe commanding the legions
sent forth from Mordor, it is a dark day for the free peoples
of Middle-earth; one which may yet see their lands fall into
permanent shadow...

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content:
MINAS MORGUL
MINAS MORGUL
O
n the western border of Mordor lies the dead city
of Minas Morgul, home of the Nazgûl and a great
fortress of Mordor. Yet, Minas Morgul was not always
the blighted city it is now, it was formerly a stronghold of
Gondor. Known as Minas Ithil, the fortress acted as the
first great bastion against the armies of Mordor, a stalwart
line of defence put in place to keep the armies of the Dark
Lord at bay.
That all ended when the Nazgûl descended upon the city,
conquering it with their sorcerous might and transforming
it into a place of dread. Now shrouded in darkness, Minas
Morgul gives off an eerie green glow and has an evil feel
to it. Those who stray too close to Minas Morgul are said
to be overcome with a sense of great dread, for the Nazgûl
have dwelt there for so long that their malign influence has
seeped into not just the very city itself but also corrupted the
surrounding lands.
Many stationed within Minas Morgul have also been imbued
with the malign sorceries of the Nazgûl, their weapons
seemingly more potent the longer they have lingered within
the city. Alongside them march Orcs from the Morannon who
stopped at the dead city before marching upon Osgiliath.
These Orcs make for a formidable fighting force - the innate
strength of those from the Morannon complementing the
sinister weaponry of those who have long dwelt there.
Not all of Minas Morgul's armies are of the living. Ghostly
spectres are said to have been seen alongside the Orcs,
tempting the living to stray from the path and into harm.
Yet the deadliest warriors of Minas Morgul are undoubtedly
the Nazgûl, and, above all, the Witch-king of Angmar. As
Sauron's most fearsome servant, the Witch-king leads the
armies of the Dark Lord into battle from atop his dreaded Fell
Beast, and when he rides out from Minas Morgul, the Witch-
king is at the height of his power.

CIRITH UNGOL
W
ithin the western mountain face of Mordor,
near to the fortress of Minas Morgul, lies the
high pass of Cirith Ungol, a path into Mordor that is said
to contain a nameless terror that will feast upon all who
attempt to cross. Upon the other side of the pass is the
tower of Cirith Ungol, a fortification garrisoned by Orcs
and Mordor Uruk-hai ever watchful should any enemies of
the Dark Lord, or even something fouler, try to enter Mordor
by that route.
Within the tower of Cirith Ungol are stationed both Orcs
and Uruk-hai, each led by cruel and savvy leaders. Gorbag
commands the Orcs within Cirith Ungol; an intelligent and
savage Orc, Gorbag will stand up to the stronger Uruk-hai
should his authority be questioned. Unlike most of his kind,
Gorbag knows he can use his situation to his own advantage,
and will often use his cunning to convince an unwitting Uruk-
hai to act to his own benefit should he need to.
The Mordor Uruk-hai are led by Shagrat, the strongest Uruk
within the garrison. Whilst he may not possess the same
intellect as his Orc counterpart, Shagrat will crush any
resistance to his command with utter cruelty. Though the
Orcs and Uruk-hai are stationed to work together, both
harbour a great disdain for the other, constantly seeking to
undermine their counterpart. With tension on a knife-edge, it
wouldn't take much for the Orcs and Uruk-hai to turn against
each other; and should they be forced to fight alongside their
rivals, each will seek to outdo the other.
The high pass itself is home to Shelob, the spawn of
Ungoliant. This giant spider-like creature is a ravenous
being that will eagerly feast upon any unfortunate beings
that she would come across, whether they be Orcs, Uruk-hai
or perhaps something more appetising. Those who Shelob
marks out to be her prey will likely have no idea they are being
stalked, only finding out when it is already too late...

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content:
THE BLACK GATE
THE BLACK GATE
W
ith the Battle of Pelennor Fields over, the forces
of Mordor have been driven back to the dark
lands, and the captains of the West are preparing to march
upon Mordor. Yet even as they do, the forces of the Dark
Lord are regrouping. Behind the Ash Mountains, legions
of Orcs are gathering; every stronghold and Orc camp has
been emptied with all of them now ready to confront the
army that dares to challenge the Dark Lord so openly.
As the Black Gate opens, the Mouth of Sauron rides out. An
emissary of the Dark Lord himself, this Black Númenórean
greets the captains of the west with proclamations of Frodo's
demise, before the full might of Mordor is unleashed upon
them. From the bowels of the dark lands vast legions of Orcs
lurch into battle, driven onwards by the implacable will of
their master. The Orcs are accompanied by huge, heavily
armoured Trolls that tower above their foes and carry great
weapons capable of splitting their enemies in two.
At the head of the forces at the Black Gate is a hulking Mordor
Troll Chieftain, larger and more bloodthirsty than any of its
kind. This great Troll is easily capable of besting the mightiest
heroes of the free peoples, swatting them aside in the name
of the Dark Lord. With such a beast at the head of the armies
of the Black Gate, any hero that stands against it will need a
stout heart, an unflinching resolve and every ounce of skill
they can muster if they are to stand any chance of survival.
Yet it is more than just the armies of Orcs on the ground
that emerge from the Black Gate. As the armies of the west
fight the impossible odds that are spewed forth from the
Morannon, a deafening piercing shriek can be heard from
above, heralding the arrival of the Nazgûl atop their Fell
Beasts. The armies of the Black Gate represent every final
ounce of power that the Dark Lord can muster, forming a
truly formidable force that has the might to destroy all in
their path.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content:
ARMY OF THE WHITE HAND
ARMY OF THE WHITE HAND
B
efore his treachery was fully revealed to the free
peoples of Middle-earth, it was believed that the
Wizard Saruman was still a force for good within the
world, using his powers to aid those he once called allies.
However, within his stronghold of Isengard, Saruman was
secretly amassing an army, one that would be used to man
the forges of industry beneath Orthanc, and also seek to
weaken the kingdom of Rohan.
This army is made up of those who the Wizard managed
to rally to his cause. Orcs have been sent to Isengard to aid
Saruman in his schemes, working the forges and breeding
pits. Packs of Warg Riders act as scouts, traversing the nearby
lands to ensure none discover their master's plans; and the
Wild Men of Dunland have pledged themselves to Saruman to
gain revenge on the Rohirrim they so despise.
Yet it is those grown beneath Orthanc that prove to be
Saruman's most potent warriors, his first batch of Uruk-
hai. These strong, vicious warriors lead the raids on
nearby Rohan villages and settlements, leaving naught
but smouldering ruins in their wake. Such is the brutality
of these Uruk-hai that Saruman has finally decided to
reveal his true intentions, marking his warriors with the
White Hand - a precursor to the full might Isengard would
eventually unleash.
Having used his voice to weaken Théoden, Saruman's armies
now rampage almost unopposed across the lands of Rohan
as they seek to bring the kingdom to its knees. Yet Saruman's
powers are not limited to mere whispers and conjurations,
and can even be used to manipulate the elements from great
distances, a power that makes the armies of Saruman a
formidable foe.

and can travel enormous distances; it even has the power to
invoke the weather to produce terrible storms.

birds, Crebain make for excellent spies to bring word of the
enemy to Saruman.

content:
LURTZ'S SCOUTS
LURTZ'S SCOUTS
W
ithin the foul pits of Isengard, the fallen Wizard
Saruman has set about breeding his own army:
one that consists of a new breed of Orc. These new Orcs
are stronger and more dangerous than their brethren
that reside in Mordor, and their improved durability and
endurance allows them to travel at great speeds, even in
sunlight that would impede lesser Orcs. Saruman believes
he has created the perfect army - his fighting Uruk-hai.
At the head of the scouting Uruk-hai is Lurtz, the largest,
strongest and most fearsome of all the warriors under the
control of Saruman. Unwaveringly loyal to the Wizard he
serves, Lurtz will stop at nothing to claim the Elvish weapon
that his master desires, driving his warriors forwards in
search of it. Lurtz will readily take on any who stand between
him and his goal, and it would take a warrior of exceptional
skill to be able to stop the head of the Uruk-hai.
It is these relentless warriors that Saruman has sent to
track down the Fellowship and retrieve the Ring that is
carried by one of the Halflings. Making great haste to locate
their quarry, the scouting Uruk-hai relentlessly march from
Isengard, stopping only for enough rest to allow them to
continue. It is upon the hill of Amon Hen where the Uruk-hai
finally locate the Fellowship, embroiling them in a deadly
skirmish within the trees.
Bred for the purpose of hunting and tracking down those
that Saruman wants dead or captured, the Uruk-hai are a
foe that cannot be underestimated. The scouts of Isengard
are a relentless and determined force, and those who have to
stand against them will be hard pushed to stop their advance.
Should they catch up to their quarry, Lurtz will demand no
mercy as they capture their targets and hack down those that
accompany them.

them to him, no matter what stands in their path.
Friendly models increase their Move Value to 8". Additionally,

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content:
UGLÚK'S SCOUTS
UGLÚK'S SCOUTS
H
aving tracked Frodo and his companions to Amon
Hen, Saruman's scouting Uruk-hai have managed
to engage and break the Fellowship. Their mission to
capture the Halflings has resulted in Merry and Pippin
being carried away and the valiant Boromir falling to the
Uruks' arrows in his efforts to protect the Hobbits from
harm; and now the Uruk-hai make haste to deliver their
prize to their master.
With the death of Lurtz, Uglúk has assumed command of
the Uruk-hai as the strongest Uruk that now remains. Under
Uglúk's command are numerous scouting Uruk-hai, each one
armed with swords or cleavers, and some carrying bows and
quivers filled with black-fletched arrows. These Uruk-hai run
as if the very whips of their master are behind them, racing
towards Isengard with great haste and taking little respite for
fear of failing the White Wizard.
The Orcs that have joined Uglúk's party have been sent to
ensure that the prize they carry is delivered. At the head of the
Orcish ranks is Grishnákh, a wily Orc who detests the Uruk-
hai and would gladly see them stuck with his own blade. This
animosity is shared by all the Orcs that join him, including
Snaga, a cunning Orc who spends most of his time looking
out solely for himself and is always seeking an opportunity to
further his own agenda.
This band of Orcs and Uruk-hai are only held together by
the instructions of their masters, and they all harbour great
disdain and distrust for each other. This manifests itself as
a power struggle, with both Orcs and Uruk-hai alike trying
to prove that they are strongest and most ruthless by slaying
the most enemies; and they will fight all the harder to do
so if the other is watching, no doubt sneering and making
comments nearby.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content:
SPECIAL RULES
"Their pace has quickened" - Under the orders of Saruman,
the Uruk-hai will march ceaselessly to find the Halflings and

Additionally, friendly Uruk-hai models gain the Woodland
Creature special rule.
"Get a fire going" - When required to rest, the Uruk-hai will
make camp and secure the area while they take a breather.
Once per game, in Scenarios that use Objective Markers,

Animosity - The Orcs and Uruk-hai harbour a great disdain
for one another and will take any chance to prove they are
better than the other.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content:
WOLVES OF ISENGARD
WOLVES OF ISENGARD
F
ollowing the burning of the Westfold at the hands
of Uruk-hai and Dunlendings, Théoden makes the
decision to move his people to the sanctuary of Helm's Deep.
Upon hearing of the king's plan from his lackey Gríma
Wormtongue, Saruman sends forth his Warg Riders to
assault them on the road; for there they will be weakest and
will be escorting women and children, making them all the
more vulnerable.
At the helm of these Warg Riders is Sharku, a battle-scarred
veteran and devious Orc who fights from atop the back
of a vicious Warg. Sharku leads the Wolves of Isengard
into battle from the front, his own reckless fighting style
means he thrusts himself into the thick of battle without
much forethought, using his sharpened riding dagger to
carve through the armour and flesh of those that stand
against him.
Within Sharku's pack are bands of Warg Riders, each fighting
from the back of the ravenous Wargs they have dominated.
Armed with all manner of bows, spears and other weaponry,
these riders charge alongside their leader into battle. Some
Wargs remain riderless, either not yet 'tamed' within the
pits of Isengard or deemed too wild to be placed under the
control of the Orcs, and are instead loosed upon their foes as
creatures of raw animalistic fury.
It is these creatures that Saruman unleashes upon the
unsuspecting people of Rohan as they travel towards safety,
and it will take every ounce of skill and as many good Men
as can be spared to stave off the assault. Having scouted
ahead for the best means of attack, the Wolves of Isengard
will strike without warning upon the travelling Rohirrim; and
those who are unfortunate to find themselves in front of a
Warg's jaws will soon meet a gruesome end.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings

immediately Move as if it were the Move Phase, and then

this Move, friendly models may not Move within 1" of an
enemy model and therefore may not Charge. In Scenarios
where models enter the board, the selected models will Move
onto the board before the first turn of the game, treating
any roll to enter the board as a 6. Each model is treated as a
separate Warband in this instance.

in ambushing their foes.

they enter the board, even though they may not normally
be allowed to do so. Models Charging in this manner do not

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content:
Muster of Isengard
MUSTER OF ISENGARD
W
ith the Rohirrim having fled to Helm's Deep,
Saruman gathers together the full force of
his armies at Orthanc. As an army of over ten thousand
fighting Uruk-hai stands before him, Saruman instils in
them a relentless battle frenzy and commands them to
march upon Helm's Deep. It is there that they plan to wage
war against Théoden and all those who now garrison
Helm's Deep in the hope of defending it.
The army that Saruman unleashes is made up primarily of
his Uruk-hai, strong and heavily armoured warriors that
care little for anything other than the wars for which they
were bred. Possessing great endurance, their relentless march
towards Helm's Deep is swift and unimpeded. Amongst the
ranks of the Uruk-hai are groups of Berserkers; warriors who
cover themselves in blood and shun the protection of armour.
These warriors are some of the most deadly in the White
Wizard's army.
When the ranks of Uruk-hai engage in battle, they will fight
with untold ferocity, caring little for the lives of their allies
and continuing to fight even if those nearby are slain. Enemy
swords bounce off the thick armour and broad shields
of these fighting Uruk-hai, allowing them to press their
advantage and cut down the enemies of the White Wizard
that stand opposing them. Though Saruman's fighting
Uruk-hai have only existed for a short time, they possess
remarkable martial skill.
With the White Wizard guiding them, the full muster of
Isengard is perhaps one of the greatest armies in the closing
years of the Third Age. Few can hope to match Saruman's
armies in terms of numbers, and fewer still can hope to
match the sheer strength, endurance and lust for war that
the Uruk-hai possess. It would take an army led by the
greatest heroes of the Third Age to have a hope of defeating
such a force.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content:
Assault Upon Helm's Deep
ASSAULT UPON HELM'S DEEP
I
t is at the Siege of Helm's Deep where the realms of Men
feel the full force of the armies of Isengard. Rank upon
rank of fearsome Uruk-hai bear down upon the fortress,
each of them driven forwards by their unrelenting desire
to see those within Helm's Deep slaughtered and the walls
of the fortress stained with the blood of Men and Elves
alike. Driven into a frenzy by the words of their master,
the fighting Uruk-hai are a force unlike any that has stood
outside the great stronghold of the Rohirrim.
Using huge siege ladders to scale the walls of Helm's Deep, the
Uruk-hai clamber up them with great athleticism and swarm
the walls of the fortress. Clad in thick armour and wielding
weapons forged in the pits of Isengard, the Uruk-hai fight like
warriors possessed, unflinching as they swing their weapons
with reckless abandon. Some Uruk-hai are whipped into a
bloodthirsty frenzy, donning little to no armour and carrying
huge blades that can cleave an enemy in two, or force them
over the edge of the walls to the ground below.
Commanding the assault upon Helm's Deep in the absence
of the White Wizard are the captains of the Uruk-hai, the
strongest and most vicious among the ranks of their kind.
There are few who can match these barbaric fighters for sheer
power upon a battlefield, and the strength they possess can
cleave bone, armour and weaponry with a frightening ease.
To come face-to-face with these ruthless killers will result
in almost certain death for all who are not highly skilled
warriors themselves.
It is not just thousands of Uruk-hai that Saruman has
unleashed, for the Uruk-hai bring with them the White
Wizard's most nefarious contraptions of warfare. Huge
ballistae loose great bolts towards the walls, shattering stone
and raising enormous ladders to the high battlements outside
the keep. Teams of Uruk-hai bring demolition charges into
battle, detonating them in order to break stone and cause
massive casualties. The army of Isengard is one of immense
power with a single driving force - to end the world of Men.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content:
Usurpers of Edoras
USURPERS OF EDORAS
D
uring the reign of Helm Hammerhand, Lord Freca
presided over the lands of the West-march. A
conniving Man said to be of Dunlendish blood, Freca was
set upon securing the throne of Rohan for his descendants
and planned to marry his son, Wulf, to Héra, the daughter
of Helm, in order to accomplish it. It is these machinations
that ultimately led to the confrontation between Helm and
Freca; one that ended up costing Freca his life, and leading
to his son and allies being exiled from Rohan.
It is these perceived injustices and a desire for vengeance
that led Wulf to raise an army in secret, one made up of
his father's allies and those who share the same blood that
was said to run in his veins. Every bit his father's son, Wulf
commands his armies with an iron fist, playing off the Hill
Tribesmen's deep hatred for the Rohirrim and promising them
the chance to enact revenge upon those who allegedly drove
them from their homes many decades ago.
At Wulf's side stands General Targg, his most trusted advisor,
who also provided counsel to Freca in years gone by, and a
warrior of great experience having fought many battles under
the banners of his lords. Yet there are more than just the
Hill Tribes in the armies raised against Edoras, for not every
Man of Rohan is loyal to their king, and there may be some
that will betray Helm Hammerhand for the promise of riches
and power.
The armies of Dunland are filled with warriors who have
been whipped into a blood-crazed battle frenzy by their
leaders, ready to unleash their full might upon the kingdom
of Rohan with no thought for their own well-being. Under
the direction of Wulf, the Hill Tribesmen will leave none of
their enemy's leaders alive, slaughtering them where they
stand as an example of the might of Wulf and his father. So
great are the amassed armies of the Hill Tribesmen, that even
the mighty Helm Hammerhand may not be able to fend off
their assault.
